News.title: Brit among six people arrested after cops find 13 TONNES of laughing gas in Tenerife party crackdown
News.content:
WHO’S LAUGHING NOW Brit among six people arrested after cops find 13 TONNES of laughing gas in Tenerife party crackdown

SIX people including a British national have been arrested in Tenerife after police seized 13 tonnes of laughing gas in a sweeping crackdown.

Another six people are being investigated by police as part of the operation against a criminal gang planning to distribute the substance.



The near-record amount of laughing gas was found by cops alongside cocaine, cannabis and party drug Tusi, as well as five imitation firearms.

Police sources confirmed today at least one Brit was among the dozen suspects, but they were unable to offer any more information.



A spokesman for the Civil Guard in Tenerife said: “Officers in the south of the island have dismantled a criminal organization dedicated to the illegal importation, storage and distribution of nitrous oxide or ‘laughing gas’, a substance used as a recreational drug.”

They said the 13 confiscated tonnes marked the second-largest seizure of nitrous oxide in Europe.

The six people being investigated have not been arrested but are instead being probed as part of the operation.

Cops added: “Six people have been arrested in the operation and another six investigated as the alleged perpetrators of offences of membership of a criminal organisation, drug trafficking, trafficking in substances harmful to health and money laundering.”



The alleged gang had been planning to sell and distribute the substance across the Brit holiday hotspot.

Operation ‘Centro’ began when cops became aware of laughing gas consumption in different leisure areas in the south of the island.

They continued: “The investigation uncovered the existence of a hierarchical criminal structure, made up of a family-based leadership core, with one branch dedicated to the logistics and receipt of merchandise from abroad, and another responsible for final distribution on the island.”



During four searches on the Spanish island, cops seized 10,394 containers of nitrous oxide weighing almost 13,000kg, as well as over £50,000 in cash.

The raids took place in the Tenerife municipalities of Arona, Adeje and Granadilla.

Police also located 213g of cocaine, 599g of hashish, 1.4kg of cannabis and 46 grams of the substance known as ‘Tusi’.

They also found pills, mushrooms, capsules and edible preparations containing cannabinoids.

Five imitation firearms and eight bladed weapons were also seized, including several axes, electronic devices and a number of documents.



Cops said: “The investigative proceedings point to the existence of a criminal structure with clearly defined functions, dedicated to importing the gas to the island of Tenerife, receiving and storing it in different properties, and subsequently distributing and selling it through a supply network on the island.

“The investigation remains open and further arrests have not been ruled out.”

News.title: Man, 29, ‘punches through wall to assault his teen neighbor, 15, &  threatens to rape her before dragging her to street’
News.content:
A MAN allegedly punched through a wall to assault his teenage neighbor before threatening to rape and drag her through the street, authorities say.

Obed Reyes, 29, is suspected of breaking into the 15-year-old’s apartment and attacking her as she fought back in front of two horrified children, according to cops.



The Georgia local allegedly knocked a hole into the sheetrock separating his closet from his neighbor’s flat at an apartment complex.

The terrifying ordeal is said to have unfolded in Gainesville on August 5.



Reyes is accused of grabbing the teen, threatening to sexually assault her and punching her several times.

The teen is understood to have bravely fought off the suspect.

read more us news BEACH BLOODSHED Beachgoer pushes pregnant fiancée to safety during ‘bloody’ shark attack

She fled the apartment but was chased by Reyes before he allegedly pulled her back by her hair.

Panicked bystanders heard her screams ring out through the complex before calling police.



Local cops rushed to the scene and arrived at 10pm local time.

They saw Reyes allegedly assaulting the teenage girl before pulling him away and arresting him.

The suspect left a large hole in the wall between the two apartments.

He is said to have used the gap to sneak into a closet in a room the teen was in with two younger relatives, aged five and seven, authorities say.

Reyes was charged with burglary, aggravated assault, attempted rape, kidnapping, and two counts of cruelty to children.



He is also facing an immigration charge, although his status is not known.

Gainesville Police Chief Jay Parrish said: “I commend the witnesses’ quick response of calling 911 to get our officers there in time to prevent further torment and trauma of the victim.

“‘See something, say something’ goes a long way in our community and we are grateful to have a community that looks out for each other.

“Our officers did an excellent job removing a violent criminal off the streets, and that was just the beginning.

“The victim has a long road of recovery ahead following such traumatic events and we hope our community can surround her with that support.”



Reyes is being held without bond at the Hall County Jail, according to court records viewed by The New York Post.

News.title: Light aircraft crashes at historic airfield during show as pilot seriously injured
News.content:
PLUNGE SCARE Light aircraft crashes at historic airfield during show as pilot seriously injured

A LIGHT aircraft has crashed at a historic airfield as the pilot is left with serious injuries.

Emergency services scrambled to Stow Maries Great War Aerodrome in Essex at around 2.55pm.

Essex Police raced to the scene after reports of an incident involving a light aircraft during an air show.

The pilot, the sole occupant of the aircraft, was rushed to hospital after sustaining serious injuries.





No other injuries have been reported at the aerodrome, which was the birthplace of the RAF and used in WW1 to counter attacks from German Zeppelins and bombers.

Cops have urged members of the public to avoid the area to allow the first responders to carry out their work.

In a statement on social media, the aerodrome said: “Following the earlier incident at Stow Maries Great War Aerodrome, we can now confirm that the pilot of the Turbulent aircraft has been taken to a London hospital and is receiving treatment for his injuries.

“The site remains closed to the public.”



A spokesperson from Essex Police said: “Those attending the event are urged to follow the instructions of organisers and emergency service personnel.

“The public are asked to please avoid the area to allow responders the space to work at the scene.”

News.title: Boy, 12, rushed to hospital with life-changing injuries after being hit by car as ‘drink & drug driver’ arrested
News.content:
HORROR CRASH Boy, 12, rushed to hospital with life-changing injuries after being hit by car as ‘drink & drug driver’ arrested

A 12-YEAR-OLD boy has been rushed to hospital with life-changing injuries after being hit by a car as cops make one arrest.

Police said the collision occurred in Marlow, Buckinghamshire, at around 7.50pm on Saturday.

The crash was between a grey Mercedes AMG and a 12-year-old boy on Station Road.

Thames Valley Police has arrested a 28-year-old man from Slough on suspicion of driving while over the alcohol and drug limit and causing serious injury by dangerous driving.





The force said the boy was in a stable condition in hospital but had suffered life-changing injuries.

They are now appealing for witnesses and anyone with information to come forward.

Investigating officer Sergeant Richard Martin of the Roads Policing Unit said: “This collision has left a young boy with serious, life-changing injuries and our thoughts are with him and his family at this incredibly difficult time.

“We are carrying out a thorough investigation and are appealing to anybody who witnessed the collision, or who saw a grey Mercedes AMG in the Station Road, High Street or Marlow Road areas before the incident, to please come forward.

“Even the smallest detail could prove vital in helping us establish exactly what happened. If you have any information, dash-cam footage or CCTV that may assist our investigation, please get in touch.”

Anyone with dash-cam footage, CCTV or doorcam footage is urged to contact the force by calling or via their website quoting reference number 43260424255.

News.title: My brother’s been in jail for 14yrs for stealing a PHONE… Burnham is freeing killers but not him
News.content:
SYSTEM FAILURE My brother’s been in jail for 14yrs for stealing a PHONE… Burnham is freeing killers but not him

THE sister of a man who’s been locked up for 14 years for stealing a mobile phone due to a legal loophole has urged Andy Burnham to finally let him go free.

Dad Thomas White was jailed for a minimum of two years in 2012 as part of the now-abolished Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) scheme after taking the device from two Christian missionaries during a street robbery while drunk.



It was the “final straw” after years of petty crimes, but four months after he was locked up, IPPs – designed to ensure certain offenders could only return to the community if a Parole Board officially certified they were no longer a threat – were scrapped.

But the abolishment wasn’t retroactive, meaning Thomas, 43, is among 2,329 IPP lags convicted of often non-violent crimes stuck with their Catch-22 sentence, without a maximum term, fearing they’ll never be freed.



New Prime Minister Burnham has put sorting the overcrowded prison system at the forefront of his agenda – with Labour’s early release scheme desperately looking to free up jail space.

This could see controversially cutting short the terms of serious offenders – including two of the teens convicted over the death of PC Andrew Harper in 2019.

More than 70,000 prisoners have been let out of jail under the scheme – but since taking office Burnham has vowed to keep the most serious offenders, such as rapists, behind bars.



Killers convicted of manslaughter however are not exempt – so could walk free.

He has ordered Ministry of Justice-led reviews into the early release programme, which has been paused until October, as well as IPPs.

Clara, 44, from Manchester, told The Sun: “It has to be a matter of urgency.

“The Prime Minister should go even further. He should get rid of this (retroactive IPPs), let this sentence be gone once and for all.”

She added: “What really is this review? It’s all about looking to ease the prison crisis, it’s not about reviewing it for humanity’s sake.



“These IPP prisoners and their families have had their lives stolen and it might be too late.”

Heartbreakingly, due to the indefinite nature of his sentence and severely deteriorating mental health, Thomas was barred from seeing his son Kayden, who turns 17 in November, for more than a decade – before they were finally reunited in May 2024 following an intervention by former Home Secretary Lord David Blunkett.

Blunkett had originally introduced the IPPs but later condemned them.



On seeing his dad for the first time since he was a baby at HMP Manchester, Kayden, then 14 – who is in the full custody of Thomas’ mum Margaret – jumped up and hugged his dad, with the embrace lasting several minutes.

Clara called the reunion a “victory”, and said “our prayers have been answered”, but admits there’s a long way to go.

The dad-of-one is currently one of 2,329 such inmates stuck in limbo in prisons across the UK, waiting to be deemed fit to return to society – with official data figures showing 96 IPP lags have taken their own lives in prison, reports The Times.

Frustratingly, they must have their progress reviewed through offending behaviour programmes – but are often pushed to the back of the queue in favour of inmates who have clearer release paths.

But Clara says Thomas and many other IPP inmates have become so institutionalised and mentally unstable due to no end in sight over many years, they struggle to engage.



Clara, who became an ordained pastor last year, said: “You can tell an IPP in a prison a mile off.

“Just look for the most frail one and look at the one that’s got no soul in the eyes.”

Referring to Thomas, she said: “If he doesn’t die by suicide, his body will shut down. His mind’s already shut down.”



Thomas has been shipped to 13 different prisons during his time inside – and in 2016 had a breakdown, resulting in him believing he was Jesus Christ.

While speaking on the phone to Clara and their mum Margaret he would often begin reciting Bible scripture and speaking in Roman numerals.

For a period, he’d distanced himself from the family, which coincided with spending weeks at a time in segregation, but on resuming visits, they were shocked to find he’d grown out his hair and had a full beard, was wearing a makeshift tunic, made from bed sheets, and was weighing an estimated seven stone.

Margaret had to ask prison staff which one her son was, his change in appearance had been so drastic.

Clara said: “She picked his chin up and she identified my brother by his eyes.” Horrified, from that point the family began to publicise his cause and that of other IPP inmates, including working with former Tory MP for Bury North James Daly.



“The state has shown brutality at its highest with the IPPs,” she said.

“It’s not talked about. It was abolished in 2012, but these prisoners are out of sight, out of mind.”

Overtime, Thomas has developed severe psychosis and paranoid schizophrenia, including leading him to attempt setting himself alight.

As a result, in recent months, he has been moved to a psychiatric hospital in Northamptonshire – with Clara travelling 160 miles from Manchester to see him.

Alopecia has left large patches of hair missing, while one of his eyebrows is almost completely gone.



She said: “I sat on his chair with him and I held him. And he was trying not to show the staff his tears and I was wiping his tears and I said, ‘what’s wrong? Tell me’.

“He couldn’t connect the tears to the feeling of emotion and he couldn’t actually tell me. Then he met me with biblical scripture.

“The hospital says that he uses that as a shutting down mechanism. But the way I see it, he uses that to save his bloody life.”

Clara says she lies in bed at night having “flashbacks” to how “hopeless” Thomas seemed during that last visit, and hasn’t been able to bring herself to see him again.

She said due to Thomas not engaging with psychiatrists at the hospital, the family have been told he will soon be moved back into a 14th different prison. It could be any day now.



“They may as well say there’s no cure for your brother. So we’re going to send him back now,” she said.

Clara, who grew up with three siblings in poverty in Manchester’s Moss Side, said her Thomas had begun getting involved in petty crime from the age of 12, beginning with shoplifting and stealing bicycles.

From 2004 onward he accumulated a record of 16 convictions for theft and robbery.

After robbing the mobile phone in early 2012, aged 28, his convictions totted up triggering the “dangerousness” clause in the justice system at the time resulting in the IPP.

“These men don’t know if they’re going to live or die – not all of them are going to cross the finish line, they’re not all going to survive this, and my brother’s certainly not excluded.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said: “It is right that these sentences were abolished, and as the IPP annual report shows, support has significantly improved for these offenders, with greater access to rehabilitation and mental health support. We are now looking at what more can be done.

“As we have set out, the Justice Secretary is reviewing reforms to these unjust sentences.”

News.title: Prostitutes in pink lycra, men at all hours & strangers in our homes… how brothel turned quiet street into nightmare
News.content:
RED BLIGHT Prostitutes in pink lycra, men at all hours & strangers in our homes… how brothel turned quiet street into nightmare

RESIDENTS have told how their lives were turned upside down after a suspected brothel opened on their once quiet street.

Neighbours told The Sun how men would “line up” outside at all hours, they spotted scantily clad suspected sex workers – and at times saw strangers walk into their properties having got the wrong address.



Cops have since raided the alleged sex den – along with another nearby – and arrested four people for prostitution.

Police shut down the sites in Oldham – stating their presence was causing “considerable distress” to locals.



At one property, a “welcome” sign hangs outside the front door while a tall hedge obscures much of the front of the property.

Residents living near to the three-bedroomed house in Oldham claimed men would arrive throughout the day and night.



“Men would be coming and going at all hours,” said Darren Hall, 51.

“I have to leave for work quite early, around 4am, and I’ve seen men coming out at that time.



“Some have mistaken my house for the brothel and one day I even had one man walk through my front door.

“I was a bit shocked and just looked at him and said, ‘What you doing here?’”

Darren claims the brothel was previously a cannabis farm.

“One neighbour has decided to sell up and move out because she’s so fed up,” he said.

“It’s not the kind of thing you want on your doorstep.”



He added that he’d occasionally see people at the property he believed were sex workers.

But he was able to glimpse inside one time and was surprised to see “bright, flashing LED lights” lining the staircase, apparently “directing” visitors upstairs.

At the back of the property, there’s a conservatory containing a scruffy settee, table and chairs and a bottom bed while empty bottles of alcohol had been stuffed into plastic bags.



A woman, who’s lived on the road for 55 years but didn’t want to be named, said random cars and taxis would regularly arrive late a night and men could be seen, “wandering up and down” the road.

“I’d be watching TV and I’d see someone go past the window in the road outside.

“You could tell they were looking for somewhere.

“Sometimes, they’d be on the phone talking to someone and the next minute a woman would appear at an upstairs window [of the brothel} and she’d wave and gesticulate as if to say, ‘We’re over here.’

“This could happen day or night but after dark it became really busy,”



She added that she had spotted women at the door of the address “dressed in leggings” and “pink lycra”.

Another resident said she had spoken to the suspected sex workers, who appeared to be Eastern European, and they were “nice and friendly”.

But she said she had concerns they were “vulnerable” and were being “exploited”.

“I’ve seen lots of men walking up and down the road looking for the right house,” she said.

“It made me worried to take the dog for a walk at night.



“And I kept on thinking that someone might turn up in my back garden.”

At the second brothel, a terraced home around five miles away, curtains emblazoned with palm trees hang from the front window and rubbish is piled up in bins.

Residents described seeing police raid the property and man, who’d tried to flee out the back, being arrested.

One resident said: “As far as I know, only the woman lived there.

“She told me she did Chinese massages. But I had no idea other stuff was going on there – I was very surprised.”



Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said both properties have been ordered to close for three months after they were identified as being used as brothels and it’s an offence to enter them.

The force was granted closure orders by magistrates after suspicious activity was reported by residents, councillors and partner agencies.

Neighbourhood Inspector for Oldham South & West, Amie Whitehead, said: “We’re committed to addressing the issues that matter most to residents, and these closure orders show that we will act on information provided by our communities.

“These two premises had a significant impact on people living nearby, with men attending the addresses throughout the day and night and loitering outside neighbouring homes while waiting to enter.

“Residents told us this behaviour was causing considerable distress within the community and affecting their quality of life.

“We’ve responded to reports, worked with partners and gathered evidence to take enforcement action, and have now secured closure orders to prevent further criminality and protect the local community.”

The four arrested people have since been bailed pending further investigation – and had their phones seized.

News.title: Louise Haigh signed off on deafening wildfire alert – amid fury over ‘misuse’ of emergency system
News.content:
LOUISE Haigh gave the green light on sending the blaring emergency alarm for wildfires, it has emerged.

The government issued the notification warning people “not to light anything that could spark a fire, including barbecues, campfires, and fireworks“.



The PM said that the request “came directly from Fire and Rescue Services” as wildfires and blazes have swept the country in recent weeks.

The alert pinged across the country at around 7pm on Friday, accompanied by a piercing siren designed to grab attention.



However, the blaring alert sparked controversy over the “misuse” of the emergency system.

Brits were left furious as one raged online: “@GOVUK absolute abuse of the Severe Alert system, which is now being turned off on my phone.





“You’ve totally undermined the purpose of the system. Send a text, for sure, but don’t abuse emergency broadcast systems to tell us about not using BBQs.“

Another fumed: “What a misuse of the system. You hear the emergency alert klaxon and you think Putin’s finally launched the missiles, and then you check your phone and it’s the government asking you to not have a barbecue.”

It is now understood Burnham’s First Secretary Haigh approved the “most extensive use” of the UK’s emergency alert system to date.

Haigh was appointed to Burnham’s top team last month as Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster and First Secretary of State.

She was forced to resign as Starmer‘s Transport Secretary in 2024 after it emerged she had a historical conviction for fraud.



Burnham’s deputy confessed to misleading cops in 2013 after wrongly telling officers her work phone had been stolen when she had been “mugged while on a night out”.

She claimed she thought her phone had been stolen before finding it at home.

The PM chaired an emergency Cobra meeting on Wednesday to discuss the government’s response to extreme heat and the surge in wildfires in Britain.

The increase in fires came as the UK officially broke its 2026 record for the hottest day, with the mercury hitting 38.5C in Kew Gardens, London.

A total of 19 homes were completely destroyed and 18 others damaged as families forced to evacuate as the fire spread across Stourbridge, West Midlands, Thursday afternoon.



Burnham’s cabinet had initially considered sending a targeted alert to the areas in England most impacted by wildfires on Friday morning.

But by the afternoon, the government decided to scale up the emergency broadcast, based on calls from the Fire and Rescue Service (FRS), reports The Telegraph.

In a press release published shortly before the blasting notification, Haigh said: “In response to the continued risk posed by wildfires, the Government has taken the decision to issue an Emergency Alert to England and Wales.

“This is the most extensive use of the UK’s Emergency Alert system in response to an active incident, and reflects the seriousness with which the Government is acting to safeguard people and property.”

A spokesperson said: “At the request of FRS and in response to 11 major incidents and 43 active wildfires, the Government took the decision to issue the emergency alert to provide the public with vital safety information.”



Fire services have begged Brits to stop dobbing in their neighbours for having a barbecue after they were swamped with calls following the alert.

Surrey Fire and Rescue Service posted to X that they had received a “high volume of calls” urging people to call only if there “is an emergency or fire producing significant smoke”.

Meanwhile, Gloucestershire Fire and Rescue said they were also experiencing “exceptionally high call volumes”.

The Sun exclusively revealed that as panic gripped the nation, dozens of prisoners had secret phones seized as the siren sound blared.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A source told The Sun on Sunday: “Governors are laughing about it because so many have been caught with phones after the alert. It took prisoners by surprise and loads of their phones went off really loudly in cells and other areas.



“Loads were caught red-handed and it also provided loads of intelligence about where phones were.”

News.title: Gloomy UK to be soaked in rain this week after record-breaking summer – but Met Office forecasts more heatwaves to come
News.content:
RAIN CHECK Gloomy UK to be soaked in rain this week after record-breaking summer – but Met Office forecasts more heatwaves to come

THE UK is set to be soaked in rain this week after a record-breaking summer – but the Met Office says more heatwaves could be coming.

Rain is sweeping the UK after a spell of dry weather, with nearly three-quarters of England and the entirety of Wales facing drought.



It comes after the UK saw temperatures reach highs of 38C in the country’s fifth heatwave of the year last week, which saw a rare amber alert for heat issued across the nation.

However, the Met Office has predicted an increased amount of rain making its way across the country this week alongside breezier conditions.



From Monday onwards, the north will see cloud and outbreaks of heavy rain which will gradually move southward introducing “fresher conditions” with showers more widespread on Thursday.

But the national forecaster says the hot weather could return with the potential for a sixth heatwave before the UK’s summer comes to an end.

The forecast, from August 30 to September 13, says: “There is a chance that late-season hot spells or heatwaves develop, especially in the south.”

It’s predicted the UK will see “drier, more settled weather, slightly more likely towards the south and east”.



Temperatures during this period are “again likely to be near to or above average overall”.

From next Friday to the end of the month, the Met Office says Brits are likely to see a changeable period.

Many parts of the UK may see showers or longer spells of rain with the possibility of some drier weather in between as high pressure sweeps across the country.

However, low pressure systems from the Atlantic “could lead to a period of widespread rain and strong winds at times” with the chance for some thunderstorms.

The Met Office added: “Temperatures are more likely to be above normal than below overall, though the possibility of widespread or exceptional heat is lower than in recent weeks.”



This chance of rainfall comes as two thirds of the country face drought status as a result of consistently dry conditions.

According to the National Drought Group, England faced its driest July since records began 190 years ago, with parts of Hampshire, the Isle of Wight and West Sussex not experiencing rain for over two months.

In response to the drought and the dry conditions, over 27million Brits currently face hosepipe ban restrictions.

These have been enforced by nine water companies to prevent unnecessary water use.

No water company has confirmed when the restrictions will end, but it is anticipated for when water levels are replenished.



Thursday marked the second time that the UK has hit 38C in 2026, with the previous high of exactly 38C recorded in June in Lingwood, Norfolk.

The Met Office said: “The only other time this has happened twice in one year was in 2022. It also makes it the 5th hottest day on record.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

However, as Brits flocked to the beach, some regions have had cooler weather, with Scotland and Northern Ireland seeing wetter conditions.

Record-breaking heatwaves in May and June led to more than 2,800 excess deaths, with the PM urging the public to check in on vulnerable relatives and friends during the extreme heat.

News.title: Watch: BBC visits smouldering market in Ukraine after strikes
News.content:
Six people have been injured at a market in the Ukrainian capital Kyiv, as the country was hit by a series of Russian strikes.

Five people were reportedly killed across Ukraine, while Russian officials said seven people were killed there, in strikes by Ukraine.

The BBC's Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson visited the market, known for selling items like books and posters, as firefighters worked to extinguish hot spots.

Follow live coverage.

News.title: People who fled Stourbridge fires start to return home
News.content:
People who had to flee their houses during the devastating Stourbridge fires are starting to return home, as a firefighter said it was "a miracle no one has died".

Many families are only just discovering the extent of damage to their homes as West Midlands Fire Service allowed some behind the cordon after three days.

Nineteen properties across five streets have been fully destroyed. Eight households have been able to view the shells of their former homes.

Aerial images of the scene appear to show some houses have remained entirely intact while those next to them have been burnt to the ground.

Residents of Brunswick Gate, Landsgate, Ounty John Lane, Quarry Park Road and Racecourse Lane were asked to gather to speak to fire chiefs one by one.

They then learned if it was safe to return or if their home needed significant repairs or had been lost entirely.

Earlier, Dudley Council's chief executive Balvinder Heran said 96 evacuated houses had escaped damage with 85 families able to return.

Thirteen households whose properties were damaged by fire have also been able to go back home.

News.title: Murder inquiry after man bitten by dog dies
News.content:
A murder inquiry has begun after the death of a man who was bitten by a dog on a footpath in West Yorkshire.

The 55-year-old was injured in an altercation on a disused railway line off Blacker Lane in Calder Grove, Wakefield, at about 13:30 BST on Saturday. He was taken to hospital in a critical condition but died just after 19:00.

West Yorkshire Police has appealed for two people, one of whom is called Sophie, who stopped to help the injured man to come forward.

A force spokesperson said a 55-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of murder and of being the owner of a dog dangerously out of control in a public place, causing injury. He remains in custody.

Police said a German Shepherd dog believed to have been involved in the incident has been seized by officers.

Det Ch Insp Michael Cox said: "Sadly, a man has died and it is really important that we understand the circumstances of what has taken place.

"We know that two people, one named Sophie, stopped to assist the injured man and direct officers."

He added: "We would urge these two people to come forward to help us with our ongoing inquiries into this tragic incident.

"The initial altercation happened in an area used by walkers and we are urging anyone who has seen or heard any part of the exchange between these two men to please make contact."

News.title: Calls for public inquiry into Jason Arday 'witch hunt'
News.content:
Green Party leader Zack Polanski, and Labour MPs Bell Ribiero-Addy, Clive Lewis and Nadia Whittome are among the politicians to have signed the statement, alongside former England footballer Eni Aluko, National Education Union general secretary Daniel Kebede, and broadcaster Carol Vorderman.

It calls for an "immediate public inquiry into how to ensure a responsible press".

Arday, 41, was found dead at an address in Battersea, south London, on Friday. He had resigned as a Cambridge professor of sociology of education on 5 August after allegations of plagiarism and questions about some of his achievements. He had denied the claims.

Liverpool John Moores University - which awarded Arday his PhD in 2015 - concluded that he had not plagiarised work.

The row first erupted after another academic - self-defined "race realist" Nathan Cofnas, who was sacked from his Cambridge role in 2024 - said he found numerous instances of plagiarism in the professor's work. Cofnas's post had been terminated amid a backlash to his view that under a true meritocracy black people would "disappear from almost all high-profile positions outside of sports and entertainment".

Lord Woolley told BBC Radio 4's Broadcasting House programme on Sunday he and a number of close friends had met Arday four days before he was found dead at a south London address.

He said Abbott and social activist Misan Harriman were among those who gathered to offer support as they had also experienced "horrible media attention".

He said Arday felt "hounded" and the relentless media coverage had been "a bloodsport".

"Diane said to him, she held his hand, and said we will help you get through this," he added.

"But on that day, we saw a man half his body weight and desperate beyond belief."

Lord Woolley said issues of plagiarism were constant in academia and that a number of individuals, who had been accused of plagiarism had not been subjected to the attention Arday had received.

"We have to ask this question, we have to talk about - which a lot of people don't want to talk about, is racism. You have to look at negatively differential treatment."

On 6 August Cambridge announced an independent investigation into Arday's appointment.

A University of Cambridge spokesperson told the BBC that during his time at the university, Arday had received a range of support in relation to his physical and mental well-being, including counselling and support and advice.

"Our support continued in the face of intense public and media scrutiny and after his resignation," they added.

Cambridge celebrated Arday's appointment as a young black professor, one of a tiny and visible minority in academia. Only one per cent of professors in UK universities are black, making each appointment hugely significant.

More than Â£40,000 has now been raised for Arday's family, after Windrush campaigner Sir Patrick Vernon, who is also among the signatories to the petition, launched a fundraiser.

A vigil organised by group Stand Up To Racism is set to take place on Monday evening in Trafalgar Square.

News.title: Changing pubs into homes to be made harder under new rules
News.content:
The Campaign for Real Ale has previously said that pubs are being "lost forever to conversion or demolition as developers look to cash in on the desirable locations and unique architecture of pubs and social clubs".

The British Beer and Pub Association and UKHospitality have also campaigned against pub closures, with both largely blaming tax rises and other costs.

Allen Simpson, chief executive of UKHospitality, said: "The biggest issue facing hospitality businesses is costs like VAT and business rates pushing pubs out of business in the first place.

"Anything that makes it harder to take these important assets away from their communities has to be welcomed, but the government should focus on continuing its strong start on fixing the harm done to hospitality over the past two years."

In July, the Labour government said pubs, social clubs and live music venues in England will be given a 20% cut to business rates on top of rates relief announced in January.

The NPPF update being published Monday also includes default approval for homes being built around railway stations in England in an attempt to increase housebuilding numbers.

Housing Secretary Angela Rayner said: "By unlocking thousands of homes around well-connected transport hubs, we're helping people live closer to work, school and the services they rely on, while backing local businesses and driving growth in our communities."

The update also means that some groups will no longer need to be consulted on housing development plans as part of the process of getting permission.

Under the changes, Sport England will continue to advise on significant cases and the Gardens Trust and Theatres Trust will still be notified of relevant applications.

Labour has set a target to build 1.5 million homes by 2029. According to official data, external, it has so far built 392,000 homes in England since coming into power in July 2024.

Shadow housing secretary Sir James Cleverly said Labour "failing abysmally" to meet their target because of taxes and red tape.

"To try to fix their own mess, Labour are planning a power grab, seizing control from local communities and forcing them to accept development in the wrong areas because Labour won't build in the right areas," he added.

News.title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?
News.content:
Jason didn't want a "Coke can" â that's the nickname for a penis that has been enlarged with so much filler it resembles a stubby drink can.

"Some people go really overboard," Jason tells me when we meet in Manchester.

His procedure increased the girth of his penis by 16% - an amount he, and his partner, are really happy with. He says it has given him a "self-confidence boost".

"Everything still functions" as normal, Jason explains - just with "that extra little bit of width".

It is not clear how many men like Jason are having penis fillers. And you can't walk down the street and get a sense of it in the way you can visibly see the popularity of lip fillers. There is little regulation and there are no official records as anybody can start offering the procedure.

Penis fillers even became the topic of a bizarre conspiracy theory at the last Winter Olympics. Male ski jumpers were rumoured to be using fillers to increase the surface area of their suits so they could jump further.

However, some men have ended up in A&E with a penis turning black and skin "sloughing off" after a botched procedure. And the British Association of Urological Surgeons has issued warnings to men having these procedures.

So why are men doing it and what are the risks?

News.title: Friends, finances and finding your feet - advice for this year's freshers
News.content:
Journalism student Kieran Miller was worried about money, but he compared student bank accounts and chose one that gave him a free 16-25 Railcard, and signed up for student discount schemes.

Though it might be exciting to see your first maintenance loan payment hit your bank account in one big lump sum, Kieran, 19, says you need to remember it has to last until the next instalment.

With the help of his mum, Kieran, from Swansea, made a provisional budget before moving away, but warns that it's easy to get caught up in the student experience and spend more than you planned to.

"When you start uni and you're living away from your family and you've got this new sense of freedom it was also really difficult to stay strict financially because you want to make mates with people," he says. "Someone might invite you to go for food or to go for a drink - and you're like, 'I don't really want to say no because this is a chance to connect with someone.'"

As well as student loans, most universities offer a variety of scholarships and bursaries, and it's worth checking whether you're eligible.

News.title: The influencers getting bitten while chasing the perfect shark shot
News.content:
Incidents of sharks biting humans are incredibly rare, but at least three influencers have been bitten by the animals in less than a year. Scientists say they're increasingly concerned about the rise in social media videos showing people swimming too close to sharks, touching or even riding them.

"I'm seeing these videos every single week now and it's way more than it ever used to be," says shark scientist Kristian Parton, who also hosts the 'Shark Bytes' YouTube channel. "We're going to see people ending up in really serious incidents with sharks."

In July, a fishing influencer almost lost his leg after being attacked by a reef shark whilst spearfishing. In December, a Chinese content creator was bitten in the Maldives. Both incidents were caught on camera.

Researchers at the International Shark Attack File, which tracks human-shark interactions worldwide, have also told the BBC they've seen a marked increase in the past three years of people being bitten while trying to take footage with sharks.

A recent study of "swim with wildlife" expeditions, external found influencers and photographers were the most likely to ignore safety instructions.

In February last year, a tourist in the Caribbean had both hands bitten off while trying to get a photograph of a bull shark from the shallows, according to local authorities. Two months later, a snorkeller in Israel carrying a "selfie stick" was killed by sharks, reportedly while trying to get photographs.

The risk of being bitten by a shark remains extremely low: the number of unprovoked shark attacks worldwide has remained broadly stable for the past 30 years, at about 70 bites per year.

While Tayane Dalazen was bitten by a nurse shark - known as a more docile species - some influencers have been filmed touching tiger sharks and even great whites.

"We're talking about a true apex predator, a very large wild animal," says Parton. "You wouldn't walk into the Serengeti and try and put your hand on the face of a lion."

Sharks will often use defensive or "exploratory" bites when presented by an unwelcome human in their personal space, he adds.

Human interactions can also cause stress to the animals. Scientific studies have shown that approaching or touching a shark leads to high levels of hormones called glucocorticoids. These can lead to a weakened immune system, increased mortality and aborted offspring.

"If you're approaching the shark and stressing it out, whether it be in a nursery habitat, a breeding ground, or a feeding area, you're depriving that shark of an area that's important to it to survive," explains Parton, "and that's definitely a problem."

One of the best-known shark content creators is Ocean Ramsey, a 38-year-old former model who shot to fame in 2019 after she was pictured swimming with one of the largest great white sharks ever seen.

News.title: UK-made drones strike targets inside Russia
News.content:
British-made drones are being used to strike targets in Russia for the first time.

The drones, built by two separate British companies, have been used in mainland Russia in widespread and successful targeting of military and industrial targets, including refineries and warehouses of online retailer Wildberries.

The strikes, first reported by the Sunday Times, external, are said to have caused more than Â£35bn in economic damage. A well-placed military source confirmed to the BBC the UK drones had been used.

British manufactured Storm Shadow missiles had earlier been used in the conflict, although this new phase is having a far more decisive impact.

Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova has previously said drones using UK components and configurations have been used to attack Russian territory, including a fuel depot in the Kamensky District of the Rostov Region.

In April, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) announced it would supply Ukraine tens of thousands of drones, including long-range strike devices, in its biggest ever package.

The MoD said its support for Ukraine is "unwavering" and would stand by its ally "until it wins".

A spokesperson said: "We are committed to providing the equipment Ukraine needs to defend itself against Putin's illegal invasion.

"This includes over 150,000 drones this year, cutting-edge Stone Cloak devices that hinder Russian air defences and innovative low-cost cruise missiles."

On Sunday, Moscow's mayor said about 600 Ukrainian drones were launched towards the city overnight, with roughly a third of the drones being destroyed, and three people were injured.

A warehouse belonging to Russian online retailer Wildberries was hit.

Wildberries, known as Russia's version of Amazon, has been repeatedly targeted since July.

Kyiv said at the time it was targeting logistics hubs used by Russians to buy military equipment and disrupting supplies to the Russian army.

News.title: Reform proposes £50bn welfare bill cut with changes to disability payments for millions
News.content:
Reform UK says it would aim to cut about Â£50bn from the benefits bill and scrap the disability payments system, Pip, if it comes in to government.

Robert Jenrick, the party's treasury spokesperson, said the plans, to be set out in full on Monday, would be the most comprehensive overhaul to the welfare system in a generation and affect nearly three million people.

In an article for the Sunday Telegraph, external he said the current system is "suicidal empathy" and "a strange perversion of compassion".

Labour said it was "fantasy economics, built on stripping support from disabled people", while the Conservatives called it a "half-baked policy" and another "attempt to distract from" questions about the Â£5m gift party leader Nigel Farage received.

Reform's plans include making companies pay for any employees off sick for the first two years. Businesses with more than five employees would have to take out insurance to cover the cost.

Reform says this is modelled on the Dutch system and would incentivise employers to make adaptions and encourage people back to work to reduce their insurance premiums.

The party says they would cut the National Insurance contributions (NICs) paid by employers to offset the cost of this measure, insisting the change would be cost neutral for businesses.

In a policy document to be published next week, which the BBC has seen an extract of, the party estimates 2.89 million people would have their disability payments' removed, or modified, under plans to abolish Personal Independent Payments (Pip) for working age people.

The party would also remove the extra health-related payments on Universal Credit.

A new system, called a Health Security Allowance, would replace both Pip and the Universal Credit health element but only the most "severe, enduring and high-risk cases" would receive cash support, the document says.

Other claimants would be supported through a council-run programme to cover what Reform said would be the "verifiable additional costs" as a result of their disability.

To boost available support for people out of work, the party says it would spend an extra Â£1.85bn a year on interventions such as cognitive behavioural therapy, physiotherapy, and employment support.

Reform also wants to reform children's benefits, and is promising to align the system for anxiety, depression and ADHD in young people with its changes to the adult system. But this would only apply to new claimants.

News.title: 'Number of fatalities' and four injured after car drives on wrong side of motorway
News.content:
A number of people have died and four people have been taken to hospital following a two-vehicle crash in County Kildare.

The collision occurred on on the M9 Northbound at Junction 3 at about 03:00 local time on Sunday.

GardaÃ­ (Irish police) said a vehicle had been travelling on the wrong side of the carriageway when a head on collision occurred with a second car. They said there were a "number of fatalities".

The driver and front passenger, both female and aged in their 30s, of the second car have been removed from the scene to Tallaght University Hospital and both remain in critical condition.

A female rear seat passenger, aged in her 20s, was taken to St. Luke's General Hospital and is in a serious condition.

The third passenger, who is a child, has been removed to Children's Health Ireland at Crumlin and is in a serious condition.

The section of the M9 from Junction 3 to Junction 4 northbound and southbound remains closed with local diversions in place.

Irish broadcaster RTÃ have reported that gardaÃ­ said there was no pursuit taking place when the collision occurred.

GardaÃ­ said FiosrÃº (the Office of the Police Ombudsman) has been notified of the incident.

FiosrÃº's on-call team of investigators attended the scene and an independent investigation is ongoing.

The watchdog said a FiosrÃº investigation relates to incidents involving contact with gardaÃ­ where a member of the public has died or been seriously injured.

It said a referral does not necessarily mean a garda or gardaÃ­ have been accused of wrongdoing.

"Instead, it means that FiosrÃº should independently investigate the incident to ascertain whether or not the act or omission of a garda or gardaÃ­ may have resulted in the death of, or serious harm to, a person," it added.

News.title: Soldiers praised for 'phenomenal job' helping crews tackle wildfires
News.content:
A chief fire officer has praised soldiers for supporting crews tackling wildfires in south Wales.

Fin Monahan said South Wales Fire and Rescue Service was under severe pressure and very grateful to seven other fire services and the military for help.

About 200 members of the Queen's Own Gurkha Logistic Regiment, with support from 22 Royal Engineers, Royal Logistics Corp and Army helicopters have been been involved.

Crews from London, Cumbria and elsewhere have also been providing support.

Monahan told the BBC the UK and Welsh governments took "a very serious step" in bringing in the military but the "extra capacity" was needed as crews fought dozens of fires across the country.

He said his firefighters have "very specialist skills" to tackle wildfires with military assistance enabling him to "focus all of that in the right place".

Soldiers have been providing logistical support, including water distribution, to assist firefighters and specialist responders.

Monahan described the soldiers as "doing an utterly phenomenal job digging trenches and also helping us build fire breaks".

"That has liberated lots of our firefighters to go and do their more specialist skills of firefighting."

News.title: Ariana Grande leaves problems at home as her tour hits the UK
News.content:
It feels inconsiderate of Ariana Grande to bring a tour called Eternal Sunshine to the UK at the tail end of the year's fifth heatwave. Haven't we suffered enough already?

But the fans packed into London's O2 arena on Saturday night didn't seem to care about the heat and the sweat.

They came ready to dance. Thousands of them, dressed in cat ears, bridal gowns and elaborate floral headpieces.

They scream when she references rumours she's back together with her ex, Ricky Alvarez. And they bounce in unison when she plays colourful club anthems like Into You and Break Free.

It's the first time Grande has played in the UK since 2019, partly because of Covid, but also because of her Oscar-nominated role in the movie musical Wicked.

She rewards fans with a few of Glinda's signature hair tosses, external and, more importantly, a two-hour show that highlights the incredible agility of the star's voice.

Sure, the production has all the paraphernalia a major pop tour - big sets, plumes of smoke, inspired choreography - but there are long stretches where it's just Grande on stage with her band. Her stunning, four octave vocals come first. Everything else is a distant second. And rightly so.

If you dig around on Grande's YouTube channel, there's a famous video of her recording the song Positions, external, directing her sound engineers as she layers vocal harmonies and ad libs, finding new note combinations on the fly.

It's a bravura performance that showcases her facility with melody and arrangement - and she essentially recreates it live on stage at the O2.

After the opening run of songs, she hushes the audience and spends two minutes looping her voice. First the lyric, "I don't care what people say, it's true", in high and low registers. Then she adds short phrases: "Won't break. Can't Shake. Deep breathsâ¦. Tight chest. Life. Death. Rewind."

They become the backbone of the next song, Eternal Sunshine.

They're also the backstory of the whole show.

News.title: Parents 'watering down baby milk' over high costs
News.content:
A baby bank says parents are turning to "unsafe" practices such as watering down baby formula milk to save money.

Megan Sinden, founder of Moorside Baby Bank in Consett, County Durham, said a couple of families spoke of putting less powder in to get another week's worth out of it, "which to me is quite dangerous".

She called for a cap on rising costs of formula, saying: "It's not a luxury item, it's a basic need for a baby."

Charity National Childbirth Trust (NCT) said its recent study found nearly half of parents (48%) were struggling more financially after having a baby, and added infant formula should always be prepared according to the manufacturer's instructions.

Infant formula is designed to provide the correct balance of nutrients for babies when mothers cannot or choose not to breastfeed, and adding extra water alters that balance.

The lower concentration can cause nutrient deficiency, coupled with the reduced ability of the baby's body to absorb the nutrients, NCT said.

"In turn, this can lead to poor weight gain, growth problems, and developmental delays," the spokesperson said.

"In serious cases, too much water in the formula may lead to more immediate health problems because a baby's body is not able to safely process the excess water."

The latest report, external by the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) found the average retail price of some infant formula had increased by more than 25% in recent years.

Moorside Baby Bank opened in February 2025 and has so far helped 226 families with goods like clothes, nappies and baby wipes, which were mainly donated by the community.

Sinden, who is a community worker from nearby Stanley, said the bank struggled to get donations of baby milk "because it is so expensive" and instead relied on grants to buy the formula in.

News.title: Unauthorised sites are growing but travellers say they are forced to break the law
News.content:
The number of unauthorised Gypsy and traveller sites is on the rise, with developments often carried out over Bank Holiday weekends.

Since April, sites in Hertfordshire, Essex, Cambridgeshire, Bedfordshire and elsewhere have been transformed, prompting legal battles and local dismay.

In January, the number of unauthorised traveller caravans â those without planning permission â across England stood at 4,950, a 73% increase on January 2020's figure of 2,860.

The summer count also shows a rise, of 44% between July 2019 and July 2025, from 3,113 to 4,471.

A senior councillor in one affected area warns there has been a "loss of control" of the planning system, while villagers living near one site likened its rapid construction to a "military operation".

The government says unauthorised development is "totally unacceptable" and that councils have "strong powers" to tackle it.

But Cliff Codona, who founded and chairs the National Travellers' Action Group, says the planning system is like a "big dagger in their back" for travellers, leaving them no option but to "break the law".

So what do travellers say is driving some to act unlawfully, and what do others think?

News.title: Britain's youngest Formula E driver says talent isn't enough anymore
News.content:
Making split-second decisions while driving up to 200mph probably seems like a crazy task for most of us.

But Britain's youngest Formula E driver is learning to take it in his stride as his second season in the series draws to a close.

Back in 2024, Taylor Barnard became the youngest person to start an E-Prix and since then he's broken several other records - including becoming the youngest driver to secure a podium, pole and points in the sport.

So what's the 22-year-old got his sights set on now? The ultimate title, of course, world champion.

Barnard tells BBC Newsbeat he feels he got into racing by the "skin of my teeth", due to the extreme costs it takes to climb the motorsport ladder.

The immense financial backing needed to become a professional driver has been long known, with stars like Sir Lewis Hamilton speaking openly about the sacrifices his family made to get him a seat in Formula 1.

And Barnard feels if he was trying to climb the ranks now, he wouldn't make it due to prices being "so blown out of proportion".

Thousands of pounds have been raised for the family of former Cambridge academic Jason Arday as members of the public rally to offer support and prepare to hold a vigil in his memory.

The professor, who stepped down following a controversy over plagiarism, was declared dead after emergency services were called to an address in Battersea, south London, on Friday.

A fundraising page set up on Saturday afternoon by Windrush activist Sir Patrick Vernon has collected more than £5,000 to assist Arday’s family with funeral costs.

Writing on GoFundMe, Sir Patrick paid tribute to the “pioneering” academic.

open image in gallery The professor of sociology of education became Cambridge’s youngest black professor in 2023 ( PA Wire )

He said: “I was one of the people who publicly supported Jason during the recent controversy because I was deeply concerned about the nature and intensity of the attacks directed towards him.

“I was also subject to media scrutiny for signing the letter of support and challenged in supporting Jason.

“Following his death, my immediate concern is now for Jason’s family.

“I am therefore establishing this fund to help contribute towards funeral, memorial and associated family costs and to provide practical support during an unimaginably difficult period.”

Vigil for Jason Arday planned

Stand Up To Racism has also confirmed plans to hold a memorial vigil for Arday. The event will take place on the steps of the National Gallery in Trafalgar Square, central London, at 6pm on Monday.

Weyman Bennett, co-convenor of the group, said in a statement: “Jason Arday’s death is a tragedy – but make no mistake, it was the result of a racist witch hunt.

open image in gallery Floral tributes to Arday attached to the railings outside Senate House at the University of Cambridge ( AFP/Getty )

“For more than a week, the right-wing press, politicians and the far right have hounded Jason with the most vicious racism.

“They are spreading the far-right lie that Black people are only appointed because of the colour of our skin, rather than our ability.

“They have blood on their hands. Our thoughts are with Jason’s family, but we are furious with those who are to blame. Enough is enough.”

Burnham calls Arday’s death a ‘tragedy’

This follows comments from Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who described the professor’s death as a “tragedy” and called for a “moment of reflection”.

Speaking to reporters on a trip to Cornwall, Mr Burnham said: “It’s a tragedy on so many levels, but particularly just for everybody who knew Jason, his family obviously, his friends. We think of them today.

“It’s not a moment for any rushing to judgement. It’s a moment for reflection, I would say, reflecting on how things came to this.

“A really sad, sad and sorry state of affairs, and I think we all today think of Jason, his contribution, and his family and friends.”

In the hours leading up to his death, Arday told University of Cambridge professor and director of the Autism Research Centre Sir Simon Baron-Cohen that he “couldn’t go on”.

Sir Simon, who spoke with Prof Arday on Friday morning, told the BBC: “He was being subjected to relentless scrutiny, including ridicule, discrediting absolutely every detail of his life, and he wasn’t coping with the loss of his career, the loss of his reputation, and he felt he couldn’t go on.”

Arday, a professor of sociology of education who became Cambridge’s youngest black professor in 2023, resigned after press reports alleged plagiarism in his PhD thesis – completed at Liverpool John Moores University – as well as other research work.

Media reports raised further questions about other claims, including assertions that he ran 600 miles within six days and raised £5.5m for charity.

An investigation carried out by Liverpool John Moores University cleared Arday of any wrongdoing.

If you are experiencing feelings of distress, or are struggling to cope, you can speak to the Samaritans, in confidence, on 116 123 (UK and ROI), email jo@samaritans.org, or visit the Samaritans website to find details of your nearest branch. If you are based in the USA, and you or someone you know needs mental health assistance right now, call or text 988, or visit 988lifeline.org to access online chat from the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. This is a free, confidential crisis hotline that is available to everyone 24 hours a day, seven days a week. If you are in another country, you can go to www.befrienders.org to find a helpline near you.

News.title: Man charged with arson after ‘around 10’ fires started in popular London park
News.content:
For free real time breaking news alerts sent straight to your inbox sign up to our breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Sign up to our free breaking news emails Email * SIGN UP I would like to be emailed about offers, events and updates from The Independent. Read our Privacy notice

Police have issued a warning after a man was charged with arson following several small fires in east London.

Emergency services responded to multiple reports of a man starting fires in London Fields, near Lansdowne Drive, Hackney shortly after 5am on Saturday.

The London Fire Brigade quickly extinguished around 10 fires within London Fields, a popular green space in the capital. There were no reported injuries.

Metropolitan Police attended and a man in his 50s was arrested on suspicion of arson, setting fires and possession of a Class A drug.

Later that day, Isaac Shozi, 50, of Bodney Road, Hackney, was charged with arson and remanded in custody to appear at Barkingside Magistrates' Court on Monday at 10am.

open image in gallery Firefighters are working in South Wales to battle wildfires ( AFP/Getty )

Detective superintendent Liz Cumber, who leads policing in central east London, issued a warning for people not to start fires with the heightened risk of wildfires.

She said: “No one can be in any doubt about the dangers of starting fires, particularly following the recent hot weather and heightened risk of wildfires. Even small fires can spread quickly and put people, buildings and open spaces at risk.

“We take all reports of this nature extremely seriously and work closely with partners, including the London Fire Brigade. We will investigate all incidents, identify those responsible and ensure appropriate action is taken against those who are reported to have endangered the public.”

It comes as unprecedented dry and hot conditions this summer have left Britain in tinderbox conditions with numerous wildfires across the country.

open image in gallery The burnt out remains of houses following a huge blaze in Stourbridge (Jacob King/PA) ( PA Wire )

Military personnel have joined crews in South Wales fighting 14 wildfires as emergency services warn that risk remains high for next week.

On Friday evening, millions of people in England and Wales received an alert on their mobile devices warning them of a “very high risk of wildfires nationally”.

It came after prime minister Andy Burnham described Britain as a “tinderbox” and a temporary ban on disposable barbecues was put in place.

West Midlands Fire Service declared a major incident on Thursday as a wildfire spread across more than 500 acres and destroyed 19 homes in Stourbridge.

It was one of several blazes to ravage the UK this week as temperatures soared and the hottest day of the year was recorded.

News.title: Fate of iconic stadium in Miami to be decided years after Jimmy Buffett’s appeal
News.content:

The Miami Marine Stadium, a landmark of midcentury Brutalist design distinguished by its sweeping cantilevered roof and views of the city skyline, opened in 1963 as the nation’s only venue built specifically for powerboat racing.

Designed by a young Cuban refugee, the historic structure famously served as the backdrop for Elvis Presley’s 1967 movie Clambake and hosted memorable performances on its floating stage by artists including Gloria Estefan and the late Jimmy Buffett.

However, after suffering severe damage from Hurricane Andrew in 1992, the 6,500-seat facility was closed. It has since fallen into disrepair, surrounded by security fencing and covered in graffiti, despite its inclusion on the U.S. National Register of Historic Places.

On Tuesday, voters will decide on a measure that would permit the city to team up with a private firm to restore the waterfront stadium, located on Virginia Key across Biscayne Bay from downtown Miami.

open image in gallery The stadium has been abandoned since 1992, when it suffered serious damage during Hurricane Andrew ( AP Photo/David Fischer )

Over the years, the venue played host to notable civic and political gatherings. President Richard Nixon and Sammy Davis Jr. shared the stage there during a 1972 campaign rally, and local residents regularly gathered for Easter sunrise services as well as celebrations honoring Our Lady of Charity, a figure deeply revered by many Cubans and Cuban Americans.

"It encapsulated a time period in Miami that’s incredibly unique with an incredible story that touches all Miamians," Miami Commissioner Damian Pardo said. "So this is really a place that connects with Miami at a very deep and personal level."

Architect Hilario Candela was in his late 20s and recently arrived from the Cuban Revolution when he designed the stadium. He went on to spend decades shaping Miami’s architectural landscape and led community efforts to restore the site until his death in 2022.

When the stadium was added to the National Park Service’s National Register of Historic Places in 2018, then-Secretary of State Ken Detzner praised it as "one of the state of Florida’s most unique architectural and historic resources," calling it "an ambitious example of mid-century Modernist architecture" that captured the "multi-cultural influences evolving in the city of Miami during the 1960s."

In 2022, a year prior to his death, Buffett submitted a letter to city leaders advocating for the preservation of the "little cathedral of musical fun." He recalled a 1985 performance that concluded with him diving off the floating stage into the water to join fans in boats and in the bay.

open image in gallery The 6,500-seat venue has fallen into disarray and is fenced off and covered in graffiti despite being listed on the U.S. National Register of Historic Place ( AP Photo/Daniel Kozin )

"Those were the ‘Miami Vice’ days, and Don Johnson introduced us," Buffett wrote regarding the star of the popular 1980s television drama. "WITCO Desperadoes from Trinidad opened the show, and the Coral Reefer Band finished the night with what I think was one of the most fun shows, for band and fans, that I have ever done."

Buffett's daughter, Savannah, remains active with Restore Miami Marine Stadium. The advocacy group was co-founded in 2008 by Donald Worth, who launched the preservation effort after city officials proposed demolishing the site.

"The architecture gives it the wow, the history gives it its soul," Worth said. "It’s just a special, magical place, and so many people in Miami have had such memorable experiences there."

Emi Guerra, co-founder of Breakwater Hospitality Group, which is partnering with the selected development team, suggested the stadium’s prime location on Biscayne Bay could turn it into an iconic venue comparable to Colorado's Red Rocks Amphitheatre.

"There’s just something here that can’t be duplicated, and that’s the view," Guerra said.

Addressing public skepticism, Guerra stressed that the proposal is not a real estate play for residential development. The city of Miami will retain full ownership of the venue and surrounding grounds, while the management firm will serve as operators under the city's oversight.

"When it’s something that’s historic, you have two options: restore it or let it rot," Guerra said.

Not everyone favors the proposal. Ernesto Cuesta, head of the Brickell Homeowners Association, noted that while members support historical preservation, they are concerned that noise and traffic from large events will negatively affect residents across the bay and disrupt local wildlife. He advocated instead for converting the site into a green park.

Despite remaining dormant for more than 30 years, engineering assessments show the stadium’s structure remains sound. Project architect Richard Heisenbottle, who has led other prominent restoration projects in Miami, said reviving the venue will honor Candela's legacy.

He noted that while updates must incorporate modern amenities and accessibility standards, the original construction’s galvanized steel rebar prevented serious structural decay. Completed restoration documents have already secured municipal permits, he added.

Miami Commissioner Pardo acknowledged that past revitalization attempts foundered because the city lacked the operational capacity to manage a major venue. Tuesday’s ballot question would authorize the city to finalize a management contract.

Under the plan, the private manager would transform the stadium's parking lot into a flexible space featuring public recreational areas and event space. Revenue generated from events would fund the stadium's repairs and upgrades, with the private firm receiving a management fee. Pardo emphasized that taxpayers will not bear the project's costs.

"It’s the right time to finally do this," Pardo said.

News.title: Pope Leo calls for end to violence against Palestinians amid surge in West Bank settler attacks
News.content:
Pope Leo XIV has called for an end to violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank, amid a surge of settler attacks, including a siege in the village of Qusra, south of Nablus, and a separate assault on the small village of Al-Tuba, in the southern Masafer Yatta region.

In Qusra, settlers encircled houses after cutting off water and electricity, in what rights groups say is a bid to seize more land. In Al-Tuba, settlers set fire to homes on the night of Wednesday 5 August, in what residents described as an unprovoked attack.

"I renew my appeal for an end to the repeated violence against the Palestinian civilian population in the West Bank," the Pope said after noon prayers at Castel Gandolfo, his residence outside Rome.

He also urged the international community to advance a two-state solution "for a fair and lasting peace".

News.title: Jessie J responds to dating rumors as she tells fans ‘it’s time to tell you the truth’
News.content:
Jessie J has responded to speculation about her love life in a tongue-in-cheek video.

The singer announced she and partner Chanan Safir Colman had split after five years together, in a statement last month.

The 38-year-old has now responded to reports she has been spotted on dating app Raya, in an Instagram video, posted on Saturday (16 August).

Telling fans, “it’s time to tell you the truth”, the mother-of-one said: “I updated and reactivated my Raya account on a dating app. I did. For two days, I surrendered. I just got excited and I updated my pictures,” she said, before adding that she has deactivated her account.

“I won’t do it again.”

News.content:

Gurkhas have been deployed to South Wales to help tackle wildfires as the much of the country remains in tinderbox conditions.

South Wales Fire and Rescue Service (SWFRS) said on Sunday it was responding to “significant wildfire activity” with the support of other services from across the UK and military personnel.

As SWFRS crews tackled ten large fires across the region on Saturday, around 100 personnel, including members of the Queen's Own Gurkha Logistic Regiment (QOGLR) and 22 royal engineers, were deployed for logistical, operational and planning support.

A further 100 are expected to follow, the Ministry of Defence said on Saturday.

open image in gallery Nepalese Gurkhas have worked alongside the British Army as part of a 200-year tradition ( UK MOD Crown copyright )

The QOGLR is a unit of the Royal Logistic Corps composed of Nepalese Gurkhas and British officers, a symbol of the 200-year military tradition that has seen Nepal’s soldiers fight alongside the British Army.

The special forces helped with water distribution and logistical support so firefighters and specialist responders could focus on frontline firefighting.

Water was transported by military personnel from distant sources to create a mobile water reservoir in key locations, the Ministry of Defence said. They also helped move equipment, supplies and personnel to ensure resources reached critical locations quickly.

Military teams also helped emergency services access remote and difficult terrain, improving their ability to respond to the ongoing fires

open image in gallery Gurkha’s helped create a mobile water reservoir in key locations ( UK MOD Crown copyright )

The risk of wildfires in South Wales remains high due to a lack of rain, despite temperatures easing in the coming days.

Firefighters have been working 10 or 11-hour shifts on mountainsides without breaks or access to toilets, eating meals “covered in soot”, Gareth Tovey, Fire Brigades Union executive council member for Wales said.

Deputy chief fire officer Adam Openshaw said: “The combined efforts of everyone involved in this major incident continue to play a vital role in keeping people safe during these exceptional circumstances.

“We know this is a challenging and worrying time for many people.

“Please be assured that we remain committed to protecting our communities and keeping the people of South Wales safe.”

On Friday evening, millions of people in England and Wales received an alert on their mobile devices warning them of a “very high risk of wildfires nationally”.

It came after Prime Minister Andy Burnham described Britain as a “tinderbox” and a temporary ban on disposable barbecues was put in place.

SWFRS said on Saturday evening that it had already received 736 calls, compared with an average of about 300, and urged people only to call 999 if there was a new emergency to report.
