Coventry

There’s no downside to choosing optimism, so yes, we’re optimistic. I don’t expect a top-half finish but I do enjoy how the club’s being run and believe in our ability to compete. Clearly the target is to survive, but within that, if we can showcase what’s good about us and provide a challenge, that would be a very acceptable return.

Key players/weak links The money we’ve spent is basically unfathomable, but my focus has been on those who were so critical to our promotion. Matt Grimes connects everyone in the team so we’re relying on him doing that again, else we’ll have to develop a completely new way to function. Signing keeper Carl Rushworth also gives assurance at the back that we hope will translate into points. There are questions about our strikers (which feels barmy for a team that scored 99 goals last season). It’s not complicated – we simply don’t know if Wright and Simms have what it takes to score at the highest level. Aside from signing Aurèle Amenda, we haven’t touched our defence either. It’s a bold strategy. Liam Kitching and Jay Dasilva have improved significantly, but it’s hard to ignore the notion that we’re relying on players like this finding another uptick. However, new signing Caleb Yirenkyi looks very special.

We still need to sign … We saw how vital Brian Brobbey was for Sunderland last season. A dynamic, high-status striker would go a long way towards calming the nerves about our forward line. Is Taiwo Awoniyi able to be that guy? Let’s hope so. The rumours about Fikayo Tomori are exciting. If we could bring him in, good lord.

Our cult hero is … While the returning Gus Hamer is clearly our cult hero, Milan van Ewijk is the joker of the team. You’ll find him front and centre of every celebration. But don’t let the daftness fool you; he’s a serious, serious player.

If we could sign two players from our past … The original version of James Maddison was unlike anything I’ve ever seen. His game has adapted with age, which is a shame, but I’d love some of that early ingenuity. I’d also welcome back Viktor Gyökeres. He functions far better when he believes he’s the star man. Come home Vik and bash your way to upwards of nine Premier League goals for Coventry.

We will finish 17th. Top four: 1. Manchester City, 2. Chelsea, 3. Arsenal, 4. Manchester United. Bottom three: 18. Ipswich, 19. Fulham, 20. Hull. First manager sacked Daniel Farke.

Crystal Palace

What are we expecting? Right now, it’s really difficult to say. The only key player to have exited (so far) is Maxence Lacroix, on whom we made a massive profit, but we still have to strengthen the squad so that it can cope with the rigours of going deep in the Europa League without risking our Premier League campaign – a lesson learned from last season. Lots of incoming deals seem close, but not yet over the line.

Key players/weak links Ismaïla Sarr and J-P Mateta will once again be essential, given the lack of goals in the rest of the squad. Adam Wharton will show how insane it was for Tuchel to leave him out of the World Cup, and Tyrick Mitchell will continue to excel on the left. Jaydee Canvot, still only 20, is destined to be a superb centre-back and should grow further in stature this season.

We still need to sign … There’s been some solid business already – US teenager Zavier Gozo and right-back Anan Khalaili look exciting prospects, and Evann Guessand is welcome back from Villa. But we still need a replacement for Lacroix, and strength in the middle – we had a £35m bid for Monaco’s Lamine Camara rejected. Plenty still to do. Meanwhile, the decision to swap Dwight McNeil for Brennan Johnson has split opinion: Johnson – all £35m of him – was only here a few months.

Our cult hero is … A few contenders. Mateta, obviously, chant-leader Dean Henderson and, potentially, our Brazilian attacker Matheus França. He’s not there yet, but he joined the club three years ago at 19 and has barely made an impact for various reasons. But he’s had a strong pre-season, including dancing goal celebrations – some Brazilian flair would go down very well at Selhurst.

If we could sign two players from our past … Michael Olise without a doubt; he was clearly a world-class player at Palace and has continued to progress spectacularly. And Matt Jansen, from the late 90s – a personal hero of mine; such incredible talent at such a young age and would shine in the modern era.

We will finish 14th. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Manchester City; 3. Chelsea; 4. Tottenham. Bottom three: 18. Newcastle; 19. Ipswich; 20. Hull; First manager sacked Matthias Jaissle.

Everton

Despite the £327m the Friedkins have provided since the takeover, there are still doubts about the scale of their ambition. Recruitment is tough, the process (Moyes or committee as decision-makers) is uncertain. Realistically, aiming for eighth (and European qualification) is the likely limit. Does that make Blues feel optimistic? Unlikely. The 31-year wait for a trophy hangs heavy on our hearts and minds.

Key players/weak links Midfield is looking stronger but can Beto/Barry score 20 goals between them? Tyrique George (acquired from Chelsea) is a key signing. The right side of the pitch remains problematic. A couple of youngsters to watch: Harrison Armstrong, 19, made his breakthrough last season, and, even younger at 18, Braiden Graham, the Northern Ireland forward signed from Linfield.

We still need to sign … A right-back. Jake O’Brien, who has been covering there, is a fabulous centre-back and would be perfect in the middle alongside Branthwaite. A proven goalscorer would be a bonus, as would a right-winger.

Our cult hero is … Jordan Pickford. His contribution to Everton maintaining top-flight status and his excellence in goal for England are shamefully under-reported in the media. We are blessed to have such a dedicated player who loves playing for his country, the club and his fans.

If we could sign two players from our past … Alan Ball, the best outfield player to play for the club in my opinion, never stopped running, commanded midfield, was skilful and a great passer and had a tremendous shot – he had it all, and would walk into any Premier League side of any generation. What would he be worth today? And a 17-year-old Wayne Rooney.

We will finish I said eighth last season, the optimist says eighth again. But realistically, 10th. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Liverpool; 3. Manchester United; 4. Aston Villa. Bottom three: 18. Tottenham; 19. Coventry; 20. Hull. First manager sacked Oliver Glasner, not because he deserves it, but because of the owner.

Fulham

I’m always optimistic at this stage of the summer – but there’s a bit of trepidation mixed in this time round. How on earth do you make an informed judgment on our chances when so much has changed? It’s farewell (and thanks) to Marco Silva and a warm welcome to Álvaro Arbeloa, who brings with him a new set of backroom staff, a fresh approach and a determination to write a new chapter. Seems we’re set for a new, dynamic strategy, one that’ll keep us on the edge of our seats. In a good way, hopefully.

Key players/weak links We expect striker Gonzalo García (22) and versatile midfielder César Palacios (21) to hit the ground running. The Spanish duo have followed their former boss from Real Madrid knowing that running hard is part of the deal. Another midfielder, Shea Charles (22), also joined the fold, and, as well as helping to lower the average age of the squad, the trio will be eager to discard their “promising” tags by excelling in the top flight. Arbeloa may well turn to the youth ranks too, with 18-year-old winger Macaulay Zepa one to watch.

We still need to sign … If Arbeloa gets his way there’ll be further additions, probably to freshen up the back four. And maybe a younger keeper who’s good with his feet to take over from Leno.

Our cult hero is … For humour, the Naija Boys – Iwobi and Bassey – who will no doubt continue their off-pitch antics and comedic Instagram stories, although they’re a man light now that Chukwueze has headed back to Milan. Unless someone else steps up, captain Tom Cairney remains the main man, still capable of scoring match-winning worldies after parking his antique bath chair at the side of the pitch.

If we could sign two players from our past … Obvious goal-getter up front would be Louis Saha. And the super-strong Mousa Dembélé bossing things in central midfield would suit AA’s style perfectly.

We will finish 14th. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Manchester City; 3. Manchester United; 4. Chelsea. Bottom three: 18. Coventry; 19. Ipswich; 20. Hull. First manager sacked Matthias Jaissle.

Hull

I’m very optimistic. Sure, chances are that we’ll get relegated but we’ll certainly not be the pushovers people are expecting us to be. We thrive when we’re being written off, as last season showed, and have a pragmatic manager who has us playing brilliant, transitional football which suits the Premier League. We could definitely upset a lot of teams and maybe, just maybe, even stay up.

Key players/weak links As the squad currently stands, Oli McBurnie, Mohamed Belloumi and Charlie Hughes will be the key faces. But with new signings arriving to add some much-needed experience and necessary skill, that may change. Hidemasa Morita has been an absolute coup on a free, so he may be one to keep an eye on. Full-back is still a problem position for us: there’s only Ryan Giles on the left and questions over Lewie Coyle and Cody Drameh at this level on the right. Thanks to a late flurry in the window we’ve now got a healthy plethora of young talent hoping to break through. 18-year-old Australian Lucas Herrington comes as a fully fledged international and had the likes of Barcelona sniffing around before signing for us.

We still need to sign … We still really need depth in the full-back areas and desperately need a forward or two to compete with McBurnie. We could do with some more Premier League experience across the back line, too, as well as another back-up goalkeeper thanks to Jack Butland’s lengthy injury.

Our cult hero is … Definitely McBurnie. He’s a handful for every defender and a constant wind-up merchant. The kind of player you hate to be against but love to have in your team.

If we could sign two players from our past … I would have Jarrod Bowen on the wing and Andy Robertson in at left-back. Strangely, they were two transfers I thought might actually happen this summer following West Ham’s relegation and Robertson leaving Liverpool on a free. Alas, it wasn’t to be.

We will finish 17th. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Man City; 3. Liverpool; 4. Man United. Bottom three: 18. Crystal Palace; 19. Ipswich; 20. Coventry. First manager sacked Frank Lampard.

Ipswich

Having endured the Premier League two years ago, the fans know what to expect: eyes are well and truly open. The momentum and hope we had two seasons ago was stopped in its tracks pretty swiftly once the season started. This time round, the summer’s transfer business looks of a better quality, more robust, a step up in quality, giving us half a chance of survival and a smidge of optimism.

Key players/weak links Sasa Lukic looks to be exactly the type of signing we need to be making. 30 years old, good Premier League experience to add some no-nonsense mettle and physicality. There will need to be more like him and Issa Diop through the spine of the team. One youngster to watch: Sindre Walle Egeli has just turned 20, and signed for a Championship record fee of £17.5m last August. He had an up-and-down season but has had a really good pre-season in the No 10 role.

We still need to sign … A senior striker, to take the pressure off our new, young Brazilian forward Emersonn, who was Gary O’Neil’s first signing when he joined from Toulouse for £25m in July. We were strongly linked with Callum Wilson before he went to Brentford. I do wonder whether we’ll get to the end of August and land Zian Flemming from Burnley.

Our cult hero is … Of the current players, Marcelino Núñez is probably the closest. He has plenty of credit in the bank after his transfer, last summer, from a lower league club. That said, Florentino Luís’s early social media posts mean he has serious potential in this category. We’ve already had AI farmers and Suffolk Punches on Insta & TikTok …

If we could sign two players from our past … Paul Mariner for his all-round presence at the top of the pitch. He would be ideal as the central striker in the modern game. And Matt Holland as a leader and box-to-box midfield general.

Leeds

At the end of last season Daniel Farke challenged the owner, 49ers Enterprises, to move on from just surviving in the Premier League. So this summer Leeds have broken our transfer record for goalkeeper James “next Nigel Martyn” Trafford, paid £34m for defender Tarik Muharemovic, and gone back for Harry Wilson, one of last season’s top creators in the Premier League. Over to you, Daniel. His challenge now is turning ambition into results fast enough to prove he’s the manager to move Leeds on from just surviving. A long-lusted-for new West Stand is under construction at Elland Road and the mood is good, which can be dangerous for a self-professed massive club in the bottom half of the Premier League.

Key players/weak links The main strength, and weakness, is Dominic Calvert-Lewin. He’s our key goalscorer, but doesn’t have much back-up. Left-back is similar, but Jayden Lienou is a promising teenage understudy for Gabriel Gudmundsson.

We still need to sign … The priority is a striker to help Calvert-Lewin and Lukas Nmecha. There are rumours, though, about adding more flair for the forward line.

Our cult hero is … Anton Stach’s YouTube channel is, thankfully, a delightful contribution to happiness in our world. He’s been wandering the streets of Leeds incognito asking people what they have for breakfast, and filming himself buying EU plug adaptors in Boots. On Instagram, his partner’s gameday graphics have brought Sharknados to Elland Road. Good, wholesome stuff.

If we could sign two players from our past … The correct back-up for DCL would be Luciano Becchio. To add some suaveness to our bustling midfield, Gary McAllister.

We will finish 12th. Top four: 1. Arsenal; 2. Aston Villa; 3. Liverpool; 4. Manchester City. Bottom three: 18. Sunderland; 19. Hull; 20. Coventry. First manager sacked Frank Lampard.

Liverpool

I’m always optimistic about a new season, but this one feels very much like a new beginning for us and a real unknown. We start minus a few familiar faces alongside a new manager and some new signings, but that’s balanced with Van Dijk and Alisson still being here and others who’ve been at the club a while now. I’d put little store by the pre-season results or that Iraola said we can’t run after 60 minutes – he didn’t mean it – and we’ll see how it goes when it all kicks off for real next week. We have top players, the boss comes with a style that fits in with the club and I believe we’ll do well. The target is to be up there fighting for a top spot next May.

Key players/weak links At the back with all their experience, Van Dijk and Alisson will be crucial. There’s a big gap to fill up front, but Isak now has the chance to stake his claim after a nightmare season for him last time around. Wirtz too will want to show he can adapt to the pace of the Premier League and be a force. As for youngsters, Rio Ngumoha has already shown what he can do and the more he plays the better he will become. Trey Nyoni is pulling in the plaudits for his midfield play and if Giovanni Leoni continues his recovery he too has the potential to nail down a place.

We still need to sign … Defenders. Despite bringing in a couple, including Ifeanyi Ndukwe who won’t count yet, it still feels as if we need a solid centre-back and right-back for the immediate and long-term future. Konsa or Murillo at Forest? A central midfielder to help out Gravenberch and an attacker who plays on the right – Ibrahim Mbaye has been mooted, though PSG might balk at the idea of us coming after two players, because Barcola is a done deal. Apparently.

Our cult hero is … Not sure we have one at the minute, we need someone to step up.

If we could sign two players from our past … Alan Hansen to partner Van Dijk, and Steven Gerrard to inspire and work his magic from midfield all over the pitch.

Manchester City

I’m excited; it’s a new dawn under Maresca. Naturally, every City fan loved Pep’s reign. We know we’ll never have it as good again. And I doubt we’ll ever see a more dominant managerial era in the Premier League. But after 10 years, naturally, there’s something exciting about a fresh start. The target is simple: we need to win the league back. The last team that weren’t City to retain the title were United in 2008-09. It’s our job to make it incredibly difficult for Arsenal.

Key players/weak links To temper the optimism slightly, losing Rodri, if it happens, is obviously a massive blow. He’s the best No 6 in the world, without doubt. So by definition, he’s irreplaceable. Having said that, given his age (30), the club were always planning to sign his successor this summer. And in adding Anderson and Bouaddi, it feels like Viana has done excellent business. The key players will be Haaland, Semenyo, Gvardiol, Donnarumma, O’Reilly, Cherki, Foden (if he can recover his level) and Doku. They’re the most nailed-on starters (plus Anderson). Youngster to watch? Ryan McAidoo.

But if Doku or Semenyo pick up an injury, then currently (pending the Spurs interest) we’d have to rely on Savinho. Right-back is also a concern for me: too much depends on Nunes (again).

Our cult hero is … Has to be Haaland, doesn’t it? The bloke’s dripping in aura. The manner in which he schooled Gabriel v Brazil at the World Cup … delicious. More of that please.

If we could sign two players from our past … Raheem Sterling was ridiculously good in his prime. Just relentless. He’d be perfect for Maresca’s system, with wingers isolated one-v-one. And Aymeric Laporte: vastly underrated, I think he’s still good enough to play for us!

Manchester United

Carrick is getting the best out of a group who were spectacularly mismanaged for a couple of years. The difference he made in six months was ridiculous. After the longest goodbye in recent history, Casemiro has gone, replaced by midfielders who can actually run – but we could still be reliant on keeping injury-prone Mount fit. I hope it’s not a case of Glazernomics repeating itself, where we spend to qualify for the Champions League, then go shopping in the bargain bin once we’ve qualified. Give Carrick another couple of decent signings and I genuinely think we can challenge: Arsenal fell over the line, City have lost their greatest-ever manager, Liverpool’s defence already looks shot through and Chelsea have 35 first-team players, which should present its own problems. Realistically, I think we will finish third.

Key players/weak links We are looking forward to the link-up play between Tielemans and Bruno. Tielemans’s eye for a pass will be a boon for our forwards. I can see Sesko building on a decent first season but if we’re competing on four fronts we need to sign another striker. The weak spot is still left-back. Luke Shaw being fit was almost a miracle last season, but we can’t build a season around hoping his body holds together.

We still need to sign … A left-back, Lewis Hall would be my choice. We need another striker, we will probably get last-resort Watkins on the last day of the window, hopefully a straight swap for Rashford.

Our cult hero is … Carrick. He went from being the quiet bloke in the background to dragging United into the Champions League. There’s something very satisfying about a former United player coming back and actually understanding what the club is supposed to be.

If we could sign two players from our past … Robson and Rooney. Captain Marvel in midfield for the leadership, aggression and sheer refusal to accept defeat. Rooney because he was everything you want from a modern forward: technically brilliant, ferocious, selfless and capable of playing anywhere on the pitch.

If nothing else, it can’t be as chaotic as last season. Sunderland

Tottenham

Nothing screams more “Tottenham Hotspur” than stating we’re going to have an outstanding season having finished 17th twice in succession and narrowly avoided relegation. We probably should have gone down. Somehow West Ham managed to be a little bit more rubbish than a team that could barely win home games. Our cult hero is … Djed Spence for his World Cup heroics – but we are selling him to Inter. So it has to be the Spurs social media team, the togetherness vibe is the feelgood cleansing we need.

If we could sign two players from our past … It’s a cheat code, but let’s add Harry Kane to the frontline and Gareth Bale to the wing (or any position he wants).

We will finish 17th/1st. Top four: 1. Tottenham; 2. Manchester City; 3. Liverpool; 4. Manchester United. Bottom three: 18. Nottingham Forest; 19. Newcastle; 20. Aston Villa. First manager sacked Mikel Arteta.

Sports.title: Leicester learn harsh reality of life in League One but youngsters provide silver lining
Sports.content:
If Leicester thought this season was going to be the footballing equivalent of a gap year, visiting new places and learning some life lessons before returning home, then they were mistaken. Being outfought and outperformed by Notts County, a well-organised and energetic team promoted from the fourth tier, brought the harsh reality of life to the fore on Saturday.

Russell Martin’s desire to play out from the back provided the fragile foundation of a dispiriting performance for a team tipped to storm back up. Ollie Cooper charging down the ponderous Alex McCarthy before seeing the ball bounce back off the crossbar welcomed Leicester to League One within six minutes. McCarthy or the confused centre-back pairing of Caleb Okoli and Harry Souttar repeatedly gave the ball away in and around the penalty area as the team created their own problems. Things went so badly that a compilation of their slapstick defending quickly gained traction on social media.

Jayden Joseph gave Leicester an undeserved lead, but it did not ignite an improvement and they inevitably gave away an equaliser through further ineptitude at the back as no one reacted quickly enough to a dangerous situation, allowing the unmarked Conor Grant to pounce in the six-yard box.

With most of the sell-out crowd of 17,172 celebrating their own uplift, and the rapid demise of their rivals, Leicester struggled to cope with the intensity. “We’ve got loads of learning to do and we’ll be better for that, much better,” Martin said.

This was the first league meeting between the clubs since 1994 because they have been on very different paths over the past 32 years. There was plenty of passion for this rare East Midlands derby with County back at this level for the first time since 2014-15 and Leicester fans making the short trip to prove devotion is not determined by trophies and success. They also showed displeasure at the ownership that has overseen the slide and earned the right to boo as their viewing journeyed between subpar and unacceptable.

“A bit of anxiety crept in, the atmosphere changed in the stadium, and that’s the biggest learning for us,” Martin said. “If we don’t look after each other with the ball, like we didn’t towards the end, then it doesn’t suit us.”

View image in fullscreen Jayden Joseph put Leicester ahead in their 1-1 draw against Notts County at Meadow Lane. Photograph: David Rogers/Getty Images

When Leicester won the Premier League a decade ago, County finished 17th in League Two and went on to spend four years in the National League. Leicester may think their reputation should mean they are playing on the other side of the River Trent at the City Ground, but that scenario is a long way off on this evidence.

The uncertainty among the Leicester defence was in tune with the club’s overall situation. A sale brochure has been created to market the club for a takeover, but Martin has not received word that Leicester are officially for sale, despite reports of the owner, King Power, wanting more than £200m. It would seem difficult to reach such a figure based on the distressed nature of the asset, despite a £100m training ground and players such as Oliver Skipp, who cost £20m. For comparison, County train at the local university and their most expensive summer signing was £200,000.

Among the misery, the silver lining is that dropping down the pyramid and selling off assets opens up opportunities for young players. Will Alves, Joseph and Sammy Braybrooke started and looked the most adept in difficult circumstances, while their more illustrious colleagues hid from battle. The trio spent last season on loan in either the third or fourth tier and that experience among those relegated from the Championship was an ideal fit. The expensive Premier League signings Okoli and Skipp were not representative of their CVs, while the forwards were blunt.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“I said to people it’s not going to be easy,” Martin said. “The first day of the season, we get some crazy results. This was not an easy fixture on Sky; early kick-off; a team that got promoted last year, just down the road. We take it and we move on. And we have to improve next week.”

It cannot be easy being in the Leicester ranks, with their best players being quickly sold after relegation to bring in funds and questions remaining over others. Stephy Mavididi and Wout Faes missed the match after receiving bids, while the captain, Souttar, has interest from Championship sides. Given the unsettled and youthful nature of the squad, some pragmatism would not go amiss, but that is not Martin’s style.

One of Leicesterthe club’s key selling points is, according to the brochure, their “140-year storied history”, but their efforts here will not even make a footnote. Leicester cannot assume previous success will mean either promotion or a quick sale. It is a club in a state of flux, lacking certainty on and off the pitch. If they hoped the trip to Meadow Lane would be the start of the uplift, they were sorely misguided.

Sports.title: Newcastle’s Matthias Jaissle looks on bright side despite lacklustre Leverkusen defeat
Sports.content:
Reasons to be fearful or cause to be cheerful? Newcastle fans among a crowd in excess of 39,000 at St James’ Park on Saturday had much to debate as they headed home from a slightly underwhelming 2-1 friendly defeat by Bayer Leverkusen.

The bad news is that a suddenly youthful team still coming to terms with life without this summer’s departed stars, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimarães, look more than a little undercooked before Liverpool’s visit on Premier League duty next Sunday.

Late last year these teams drew a Champions League group stage game in Leverkusen but since then the Germans have reconstructed a then transitional squad and Newcastle dismantled theirs.

Eddie Howe’s sudden departure at the end of July has left Matthias Jaissle, late of Jeddah’s Al-Ahli, to pick up the managerial pieces. Despite this defeat on a day when Leverkusen looked to be playing within themselves, the 38-year-old German is already showing a few, albeit tentative, indications that he just might be able to put one of football’s most complicated jigsaws back together.

If Malick Thiaw, Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa in particular appear re-energised by his coaching, Jaissle’s faith in the 17-year-old Mason Miley, the younger brother of the midfielder Lewis, was fully vindicated as the academy product shone at right-back.

“Mason’s a young lad with the attitude we need; he has the right heart and the right quality,” said Jaissle as he sipped an energy drink intended to replace the body’s lost electrolytes. If only he could find such a simple solution to filling the missing links left by Gordon, Tonali and Guimarães.

At least Dan Burn is still around and will be Newcastle’s captain, with Joelinton as his deputy. The Brazilian, though, is injured and will miss the Liverpool game, while Burn was not involved here as Jaissle split his squad in two during a weekend that features another friendly here, against Strasbourg on Sunday.

Leverkusen represented the new manager’s first match in charge at St James’ Park but it was hardly the ideal start. Inside a minute his team were behind.

When Ibrahim Maza manoeuvred the ball on to his left foot in the area, Newcastle’s new goalkeeper, Lukas Hornicek, was powerless to resist the resultant shot. No matter that it was only a friendly, even Howe’s normally super-confident successor looked a little crestfallen.

“It’s a big challenge,” he said. “It’s a big transition.”

Jaissle cut a restless figure as he prowled the home technical area, sometimes straying far too far outside its confines for the liking of match officials.

View image in fullscreen Yoane Wissa shoots in Newcastle’s home strip before they switched to lilac shirts, due to a colour clash, at the first hydration break. Photograph: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United/Getty Images

The good news for a coach who promises to prove more entertaining than his team – at least in their current incarnation – was that a reasonably strong starting XI improved incrementally during the first half and equalised shortly before half-time. Jaissle duly greeted Thiaw’s scoring header from Elanga’s corner with a prolonged bout of clapping.

By then he could also reflect favourably on a positive contribution from the Miley brothers. While Lewis looked his customarily assured self in central midfield on his first appearance since breaking a leg last spring, Mason’s efforts at right-back frequently frustrated Leverkusen’s Miguel Gutiérrez.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It seemed thoroughly fitting that the latter was showered with praise from his manager when, late in the second half, he hobbled off with cramp. With England’s Tino Livramento sidelined by calf trouble, Miley Jr is in real contention to start against Liverpool.

Yet in eight days’ time another right-back, Benfica’s Amar Dedic, could well have been added to Newcastle’s squad. The 23-year-old, who can also operate at left-back, previously played for Jaissle at RB Salzburg and, on Saturday night, appeared close to finalising a move to Tyneside.

Once that deal is done attention will doubtless turn to filling the midfield chasm left by Tonali and Guimarães. Although the 18-year-old Sean Steur – one of four players aged 20 or under signed by Newcastle since June – showed off some nice touches, the former Ajax prodigy betrayed his inexperience at times.

View image in fullscreen Matthias Jaissle is still working out how best to fit together the pieces of the Newcastle jigsaw. Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty Images

Players with more mature presence are clearly required but Marseille’s Pierre-Emile Højbjerg has declined a £13m move to north-east England and João Palhinha is still to be persuaded to leave Bayern Munich to plug the leadership vacuum.

On this evidence Leverkusen’s new manager, Carles Martínez, recently imported from Toulouse, might be reluctant to do a job swap with his Newcastle counterpart. Martínez’s side improved after the second-half introduction of the dangerous forward Patrik Schick and few Newcastle fans would argue the visitors did not deserve to win courtesy of Victor Boniface’s late rolled finish, with that opening created when the Nigerian expertly turned Steur.

How Jaissle, who looks to still be fathoming out how to unlock Nick Woltemade’s real yet still latent talent, could do with similar attacking incision.

Asked if Liverpool were arriving in Toon too soon, he initially replied: “We’ll do our best,” before turning upbeat. “We’ll keep using positivity,” he said. “I like these challenges. We are not concerned. I can’t wait.”

Sports.title: Scotland hope to name 39-year-old Pocognoli as successor to Clarke in fresh approach
Sports.content:
The Scottish Football Association hopes to name the Belgian Sébastien Pocognoli as the successor to Steve Clarke as manager early next week. The 39-year-old, who was sacked by Monaco in June, will become the country’s first non-Scottish manager since Berti Vogts, who was in charge from 2002-04.

Clarke’s abrupt departure came as Scotland exited the World Cup at the group stage. He had signed a four-year contract extension immediately before the tournament. It quickly became clear the SFA would turn towards a foreign manager; Jon Dahl Tomasson and Kasper Hjulmand were linked with the position.

Pocognoli will probably be welcomed by Scotland fans in respect of a fresh approach. Clarke was in position for a generally successful seven years, but was often criticised for a pragmatic style.

After a period in youth coaching, Pocognoli enjoyed a successful time in charge of Union Saint-Gilloise in his homeland. Under Pocognoli, Union won their first title in 90 years in 2025. A move to Monaco followed, but Pocognoli lasted eight months and 38 games in France.

Scotland begin their Nations League campaign with the visit to Slovenia on 26 September. Pocognoli’s first home game in charge will be Switzerland’s visit to Glasgow three days later.

Sports.title: Al Hilal target Chelsea's Pedro Neto, Aston Villa close in on Dion Suzuki after PSG transfer collapsed while Hull City launch move for Real Betis winger: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Villa close in on Suzuki

Juventus are hopeful of signing Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa despite doubts over a finger injury.

The Serie A club are prepared to make an initial offer of about £6milljon pounds, plus performance-related bonuses.

Martinez’s advisors had agreed terms with Juventus intermediaries earlier in the summer and if the Argentina goalkeeper completes his move to Turin, he can expect to earn about £200,000 a week - a significant rise on his current deal at Villa which is around the £130,000 a week mark.

Villa are confident of replacing Emiliano Martinez with Parma goalkeeper Zion Suzuk

Villa are confident of replacing Martinez with Parma goalkeeper Zion Suzuki, who is likely to cost up to £30m - but would earn substantially less than Martinez.

If Martinez leaves, then Villa would have sold three of their top earners - Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne and Martinez himself. This gives them breathing space with UEFA spending rules but also leaves the side lacking seniority, especially with Arsenal expected to make another move for Ezri Konsa this week.

Arsenal’s latest proposal was about £40m which does not come close to Villa’s £60m valuation.

Hammers turn attention to Piroe

West Ham have enquired after Leeds United striker Joel Piroe after hitting an impasse in talks for Troy Parrott at AZ Alkmaar.

The Hammers had an opening bid around £15m rejected for Parrott last week and remained in talks offering slightly more. They could yet make another offer but as it stands the deal is paused and they have enquired about Piroe with Leeds prepared to sell.

Dedic due on Tyneside tomorrow

Benfica right-back Amar Dedic is due on Tyneside tomorrow to undergo a medical ahead of his move to Newcastle.

Negotiations are at the final stages with a £29.5million deal in place for the 23-year-old.

The Bosnia international is likely to go straight into the team to play Liverpool next weekend.

Newcastle have also held talks with Bayern Munich over a move for Joao Palhinha but have other targets they are considering.

Coventry hold talks over £21m move for striker

As reported by Daily Mail Sport last night, Coventry City are in talks with Fenebahce over a £21million deal for striker Sidiki Cherif.

As well as agreeing to sign Nottingham Forest's Taiwo Awoniyi, manager Frank Lampard wants Cherif who was a target for Crystal Palace and Wrexham in January.

The 19-year-old scored three goals in 14 games for Fenerbahce.

Neto a shock target for Al Hilal

Chelsea winger Pedro Neto is wanted by Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal.

Neto is also on the lists of Tottenham and Manchester City but Chelsea's asking price is understood to be prohibitive.

Pedro Neto has emerged as a target for Saudi Arabian club Al Hilal

Tigers in for Betis star Garcia

Hull City are in talks for Real Betis winger Pablo Garcia.

The 20-year-old is valued around £7million by Betis. He made his debut for Spain U21s a year ago and has scored three goals in five games for his country at that level.

Hull have been looking for a winger after a proposed deal for Aston Villa's Leon Bailey stalled.

Garcia has become a key player for coach Manuel Pellegrini owing to his pace and goal contributions.

He came on as a substitute for Antony last night in their 1-0 friendly defeat at Inter Milan on Sunday. John Stones scored the only goal, coming off the bench to score on his debut.

Sports.title: Jamal Musiala appears to FAINT while playing for Bayern Munich in extreme heat - as new footage shows Germany star struggling moments before he collapsed
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich and Germany star Jamal Musiala appeared to pass out during his side's friendly win over RB Leipzig, sparking concern among players and fans.

The midfielder had just scored to make it 3-1 to his side in the 81st minute, but appeared dazed and confused just two minutes later before he was caught by new team-mate Ismael Saibari.

After the Morocco star lowered him to the ground, medical staff rushed onto the field as Bayern players surrounded the 23-year-old.

Amid a hush from the crowd, the medical staff eventually gave a thumbs up, with reports in Germany suggesting that Musiala had struggled with the 33 degrees Celsius heat.

Bayern goalkeeper Manuel Neuer said after the game: 'It will become clear what it was. But of course we are keeping our fingers crossed.'

Director of sport Max Eberl, meanwhile, said: 'He is fine, and that is the most important thing.'

Jamal Musiala appeared to faint during Bayern Munich's pre-season friendly victory

New footage emerged after the incident to show Musiala looking uncomfortable just after scoring his goal, and two minutes later he had collapsed.

The incident comes following a debate around hydration breaks, which were held regularly during the World Cup.

Bayern, meanwhile, won the game 3-1, with Luis Diaz, Nathaniel Brown and Musiala on the scoresheet.

Musiala, who played at the World Cup with Germany, had only been introduced as a 69th minute substitute, but had to leave the field of play soon after.

England captain Harry Kane was not involved in the game but returned to training alongside the likes of Michael Olise this week.

Bayern kick off their competitive season next weekend in the German Super Cup, when they will take on Borussia Dortmund.

Sports.title: Man United stars want Marcus Rashford to STAY at Old Trafford as Harry Maguire reveals team-mates 'hope' he won't leave the club - before lavishing praise on 'great manager' Ruben Amorim
Sports.content:
Man United stars want Marcus Rashford to STAY at Old Trafford as Harry Maguire reveals team-mates 'hope' he won't leave the club - before lavishing praise on 'great manager' Ruben Amorim

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Harry Maguire has revealed he is hopeful Marcus Rashford will stay at Manchester United as uncertainty around his future continues.

Rashford has not played competitively for the Red Devils in more than 600 days after being exiled under former manager Ruben Amorim, and has enjoyed loan spells at both Aston Villa and Barcelona.

The Spanish giants, however, opted not to make his signing permanent, and he is now back at United with it still unclear where he will be playing come the end of the transfer window.

Maguire, though, hopes it will be in Manchester.

'He's a huge threat, he's a huge threat to have in your team,' Maguire said after United's 4-2 defeat by AC Milan in pre-season. 'So if he's going to stay with us, obviously the transfer window is still open, but we hope as players that he stays and he's a big asset to have.

'I've played with Marcus for numerous years and I know that playing against him and with him in training is going to help us.

Harry Maguire (right) has revealed his hope that Marcus Rashford (left) will stay at Manchester United this season

Maguire also praised former manager Ruben Amorim, who is now in charge of the Italian side

'He can improve us. When you see when he comes on, he threatens the back line really well. He could have even scored for us today.'

United manager Michael Carrick has also suggested the England forward could stay at the club.

He said before the AC Milan game: 'He's our player. He's come back great. He's just like any other player... He gives us something a little bit different.'

Rashford came off the bench in the second-half against Milan, playing the last half-hour.

United's final pre-season game saw them come up against former manager Ruben Amorim, with the Portuguese having the last laugh following his sacking last season.

Maguire, though, insisted there are no hard feelings.

'It's great to see him,' Maguire said. 'Great to see him and all his staff. I'm happy that they're in another job and another chance to impress and to show everyone what a great manager he is.

'So I have nothing bad to say about Ruben. I got on with Ruben really, really well and all his staff. I'm sure he's going to be a success, it just didn't work out at Manchester United.

It remains unclear where Rashford will be playing come the end of the transfer window

'But when you're a manager and you put yourself in that firing seat, there's going to be disappointments and he'll be disappointed it didn't.

'But he's got a massive club now in AC Milan and myself, I wish him and all his staff the very best. I'll be following them and I hope they have an amazing season.'

Sports.title: Revealed: Man United's plot to monetise their academy after Radek Vitek's £14m move to Middlesbrough - and the two youngsters who could be next out of the door as club bosses bid to emulate Man City and Chelsea - INSIDE SPORT
Sports.content:
Revealed: Man United's plot to monetise their academy after Radek Vitek's £14m move to Middlesbrough - and the two youngsters who could be next out of the door as club bosses bid to emulate Man City and Chelsea - INSIDE SPORT

Manchester United has stepped up attempts to monetise its academy, Inside Sport understands.

There has been a notable shift within the club to put a stronger emphasis on young talent, with a view that its historic conveyor belt has slowed in recent years.

While the priority is to produce players for the first team, there has also been a recognition that more can be done to bring in funds for those who are unlikely to make it as things stand, a method deployed across town at Manchester City, and at Chelsea.

Earlier this month, Czech goalkeeper Radek Vitek, 22, joined Middlesbrough for around £14m along with a host of add-ons including a buy back clause and 35 per cent sell on, while sources have disclosed that 19-year-old left-back Harry Amass, who spent last season on loan at Sheffield Wednesday, could leave Old Trafford for a fee of around £7m, again with add-ons.

Midfielder Toby Collyer is another United feel they could command a sizable fee for, although the increased number of fixtures the club expect to play this season, following European qualification, may well increase the number of opportunities to impress for those on the fringes of the squad.

Earlier this month, Czech goalkeeper Radek Vitek, 22, joined Middlesbrough from United for around £14m

Harry Amass (left) could leave Old Trafford for a fee of around £7m with add-ons while midfielder Toby Collyer (right) is another United feel they could command a sizable fee for

Meanwhile, Amazon have commenced filming their documentary, which will be based on United’s forthcoming season and the latest of its fly-on-the-wall All or Nothing series, following on from Arsenal, Tottenham and City.

United have brokered a record fee for the production, with camera crews noticeable on the club’s pre-season tour.

Beeb under pressure over away day coverage

All would not appear to be well in the world of BBC local radio.

Rumours that bosses are set to stop commentators from covering away matches are rife, amid talk of a trial process which would mean fans of the visiting side would be forced to listen to the sometimes-parochial view of the host broadcaster.

Beeb insiders insist no decision has been made but say they are looking at working at ways to reduce duplication and showcase more of their local commentary teams across the network.

There is further angst over what some reporters have deemed double standards, claiming to Inside Sport that while some are being permitted to work for the likes of Sky Sports – and take paid BBC holiday days to do so – others have been denied such an opportunity. The BBC said it would not comment on individual cases.

British Rowing slammed for subpar farewell to performance chief

Interesting to see the former chair getting stuck into British Rowing following its markedly dry announcement of the departure of its director of performance.

Mark Davies, son of commentating royalty Barry, departed last November ahead of the arrival of a new chief executive and was quick to take his old employer to task with regards to the exit of Louise Kingsley.

A bland post, titled: ‘British Rowing statement regarding Louise Kingsley MBE, Director of Performance’ relayed the news that Kingsley had decided to retire and featured no named spokesperson or quotes.

Instead, it was left to Kingsley – who decided to go following an investigation into a complaint against her which concluded with no further action - to point out her achievements, namely turning a shambolic performance in Tokyo into a record-breaking one in Paris.

It was not lost on Davies, who noted: ‘British Rowing apparently cannot find a single person to say anything nice about a woman who turned round the worst Olympic performance for 30yrs in Tokyo to the best ever on foreign soil in Paris - an achievement for which she received an MBE. So she had to say it herself.’

Former British Rowing CEO Davies criticised the organisation for their farewell to performance director Kingsley, who turned a shambolic showing in Tokyo into a record-breaking one in Paris

Chelsea impressed by Malaysia's rising football force

Chelsea wrapped up their pre-season tour last week with a 3-3 draw against Malaysia’s Johor Darul Ta’zim - or JDT, as they’re known - and don’t be surprised if fixtures against such high-level opposition become more familiar for them.

The credit belongs to JDT’s owner, His Royal Highness Tunku Ismail, the Crown Prince of Johor, who has quietly rebuilt the club over the past decade. Visitors for the Chelsea match were left marvelling at a stadium and training complex that wouldn’t look out of place in the Premier League.

That investment has brought the club to the brink of history. JDT are unbeaten in 108 Malaysian Super League games and, should they win their season opener this Friday, they’ll surpass a world record set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas back in the early 1990s.

Having reached the quarter-finals of the Asian Champions League last season under former Watford coach Xisco Munoz, the Prince now harbours ambitions of turning JDT into a club of genuine regional and global power.

Visitors for the Chelsea-JDT match in Malaysia were left marvelling at a stadium and training complex that wouldn’t look out of place in the Premier League

Golfers fume as heatwave rounds trigger handicap hit

Inside Sport has been contacted by a number of amateur golfers left furious that their willingness to shoot a round in the intense heat last week appears to have ended up shooting them in the foot.

Scores of hackers who braved afternoon temperatures of 37C were then stunned to subsequently discover that the World Handicap System had automatically added a stroke to their scores under its Playing Conditions Calculation, which can add or subtract shots should it deem extreme conditions favourable or harder.

‘What appears to have happened is a load of those who went out in the much cooler mornings have scored well and that’s had a knock-on effect on the rest of us, who had no choice but to go out in the sweltering afternoon when it was much tougher,’ explained one of those impacted negatively. ‘Outrageous!’

Sports.title: Amy Hunt and Team GB stars caught up in armed police drama after winning gold at the European Championships as man in his thirties is arrested
Sports.content:
Amy Hunt and her gold medal-winning relay team-mates were caught up in a huge security operation that brought travel chaos to the European Championships in Birmingham on Saturday night.

Armed police arrived in significant numbers at the Alexander Stadium after a man in his thirties was spotted behaving suspiciously at around 8.15pm. He was later arrested on suspicion of fraud.

The episode caused the cancellation of six medal ceremonies inside the venue, with major disruptions erupting outside. Buses for spectators and hundreds of athletes and coaches, including the one carrying Hunt and the rest of the victorious 4x100m quartet, were delayed by up to two hours.

It is understood that police conducted searches on buses that were due to ferry competitors, staff and fans back to the city centre. As of Sunday morning, the individual arrested by West Midlands Police was still in custody.

Amy Hunt and her Team GB team-mates were held up during an armed police operation

Athletes and spectators faced travel chaos in Birmingham following Saturday night's action

A statement from championship organisers read: ‘Championship transport was suspended until the necessary security measures had been carried out whilst West Midlands Police arrested a man in his thirties on suspicion of fraud. The safety and wellbeing of our spectators, athletes, workforce and the wider Championships’ family will always be our first priority.

‘We recognise that the delays presented challenges for those affected and would like to thank everyone for their patience, understanding and cooperation throughout the evening. Further information will be issued on Sunday relating to the evening’s postponed medal ceremonies.’

West Midlands Police said: ‘A man was arrested following concerns of suspicious activity at the European Athletics Championship last night.

‘At around 8.15pm, concerns were raised after a man was found in an area of Alexander Stadium with the wrong accreditation.

‘As a precaution, security measures were put in place and transport for the Championship staff and athletes were suspended. This then led to delays to transport from the stadium for the wider public.

‘A man in his 30s was arrested on suspicion of fraud and remains in custody for questioning.

‘We understand the concern this may have caused and can confirm there was no immediate risk to the public.

‘As always, our priority is the safety of the public and we want to thank everyone for the patience.’

Hunt will return to the stadium in Sunday in pursuit of a record-breaking fourth gold medal in the 4x100m mixed relay.

Sports.title: Why a crackdown on set-pieces could leave Arsenal exposed as Mikel Arteta reveals Gunners are looking to adapt to new rules
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta hinted that Arsenal may have to adapt their set-piece routines after an influx of new rules ahead of the upcoming season.

The 2026-27 campaign will feature an unprecedented number of new laws, mostly designed to make the game flow quicker.

These changes will be deployed right through English football this weekend, including Arsenal’s Community Shield match against Manchester City on Sunday.

The laws include countdowns for goal-kicks and throw-ins, time-limited substitutions and a crackdown on holding during set-pieces.

The Gunners have courted attention previously for their physical set-plays and it remains to be seen how they will adapt to stay within the rules.

On the changes, Arteta said: ‘We have had the Premier League and the referees there with us to explain and go through everything.

Mikel Arteta has hinted Arsenal may have to adapt their approach to set pieces with new rules having been introduced ahead of the new season

Arteta's side attracted attention for their physical set-plays and it remains to be seen how they will adapt to stay within the rules

‘In pre-season we had the opportunity to see and experience some of them. We will have to see when the season starts and how this unfolds and what is more doable and what is less doable and what we need to adapt.

‘There are a few (which will have a big impact). Not being able to use the towels is already a big one in the Premier League. Let’s see what we do. Maybe we will play with hats on!

‘Something else will come up for sure. We know that everybody is paying so much to the details, all the restarts and the countdowns, that will bring someone else, a different dynamic, different momentum.

‘So I am very curious to see. They are really good rules because what we are doing is trying to promote more game time and the fluidity of the games which is better and hopefully that will work.’

Meanwhile, Arteta said he will have to elevate his level to keep up with the influx of new managers across the Premier League’s Big Six clubs.

The managerial landscape has changed significantly, with Enzo Maresca replacing Pep Guardiola at Man City, while Andoni Iraola has taken over from Arne Slot at Liverpool.

Chelsea have also appointed a new manager in Xabi Alonso, who replaced Maresca, and Michael Carrick was handed the permanent job at Manchester United in May.

Tottenham have also turned to Roberto De Zerbi, who took charge at the end of the 2025–26 season.

Arteta added: ‘We will have a lot of challengers looking at the squads, at the managers and at the clubs they are, but we know that.

‘We need to focus on ourselves and making sure that we maximise every resource we have to give ourselves the best chance. Then day by day it is going to be a long, long run.

‘Well, with a few managers as well and some new ones coming into the league that are exceptional. We know this league is full of incredible managers. It is so challenging every week to prepare games against them. That will elevate our level and my level for sure and we will try to be better.’

Sports.title: Juventus ready to gamble on injured Emiliano Martinez with £6m offer - as Aston Villa line up Zion Suzuki replacement
Sports.content:
Juventus are hopeful of signing Emiliano Martinez from Aston Villa despite doubts over a finger injury.

The Serie A club are prepared to make an initial offer of about £6million, plus performance-related bonuses.

Martinez’s advisors had agreed terms with Juventus intermediaries earlier in the summer and if the Argentina goalkeeper completes his move to Turin, he can expect to earn about £200,000 a week - a significant rise on his current deal at Villa which is around the £130,000-a-week mark.

Villa are confident of replacing Martinez with Parma goalkeeper Zion Suzuki, who is likely to cost up to £30m - but would earn substantially less than Martinez.

The Serie A club are prepared to make an initial offer of about £6million for Martinez, plus performance-related bonuses

If Martinez leaves, then Villa would have sold three of their top earners - Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne and Martinez himself.

This gives them breathing space with UEFA spending rules but also leaves the side lacking seniority, especially with Arsenal expected to make another move for Ezri Konsa this week.

Arsenal’s latest proposal was about £40m which would does not come close to Villa’s £60m valuation.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher doubles down on Myles Lewis-Skelly verdict by questioning Arsenal stance
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher doubles down on Myles Lewis-Skelly verdict by questioning Arsenal stance

Myles Lewis-Skelly has been tipped to leave Arsenal before the summer transfer window closes, with both Manchester United and Chelsea reportedly being offered the chance to sign him

View 2 Images Myles Lewis-Skelly didn't take long to impress (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

Jamie Carragher has once again questioned Arsenal's stance on selling Myles Lewis-Skelly after the Gunners star provided a gorgeous assist inside the first minute against Manchester City. Lewis-Skelly, 19, set up Riccardo Calafiori to give Arsenal an early lead in Sunday's Community Shield clash in Cardiff.

‌



The midfielder expertly turned on the ball to get away from Phil Foden before sending slide-rule pass through to Calafiori, who finished with aplomb past Gianluigi Donnarumma. It was reminder to Mikel Arteta of just what Lewis-Skelly can do - even against top opposition.

‌



Reacting to the opener, Carragher posted on X: "MLS role in that arsenal goal! Are Arsenal really looking to push him out," along with two emojis.

‌



Lewis-Skelly - who's under contract until 2030 - started the game in midfield, the position in which he finished last season after largely playing at left-back since making his breakthrough. But Lewis-Skelly's future was plunged into doubt last week after both Manchester United and Chelsea were offered the chance to sign him, with Arsenal having bought Bruno Guimaraes for £75m.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Speaking earlier this week, Carragher described the uncertainty surrounding Lewis-Skelly's future as 'strange', surmising that Arsenal want to offload him rather the player himself wanting to leave. "That's the thing that was a little bit strange about it," the Liverpool legend said on The Overlap Fan Debate.

"It felt almost like Arsenal offered Manchester United Myles Lewis-Skelly. It wasn't Myles Lewis-Skelly saying, I want to leave, or his people putting something out. That's where the shock came from, not so much the players' side of it."

"I still can't believe it. Obviously, last season wasn't great for him for the whole season, but when a young player has already put in performances like I've seen him put in at the Bernabeu (against Real Madrid) - maybe over a year or 18 months ago, at left-back, he was running the game at the Bernabeu – and then his performance in the final in central midfield against Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



"You can't play at that level unless you're pretty special at that age. All young players have ups and downs. Last season he didn't play as much as he probably would have liked.

Should Arsenal sell Myles Lewis-Skelly? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Jamie Carragher doesn't understand why Arsenal would sell Myles Lewis-Skelly (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

‌



"But his ceiling is so high for the performances he's already put in as a 20-year-old kid. I couldn't believe that Arsenal would even think about letting him go. It does feel like a strange one."

Arsenal boss Arteta was asked about Lewis-Skelly on Wednesday, with the 19-year-old having scored in a pre-season friendly. "I'm not going to talk about speculation," Arteta replied.

"If there is speculation about our players, it's a good sign. That means our players attract attention and are doing a good job."

Article continues below

The Gunners manager went on to say: "He's had a really good pre-season. We asked him to play in a different position because he played more as a No.6 - we obviously lacked midfielders from international duty - and I think he had a really consistent pre-season."

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Liverpool's Barcola boost, £60m for Arsenal to sign star, double Spurs deal
Sports.content:
All of the latest transfer news from the Premier League and further afield, including updates on Arsenal, Liverpool, Manchester United, Tottenham Hotspur and more

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's transfer live blog for Sunday, August 16.

Liverpool have been handed a major boost in their pursuit of Bradley Barcola as a result of Paris Saint-Germain signing Mika Godts from Ajax. There was speculation that the Ligue 1 champions would be willing to trim their £145million valuation of the 23-year-old, but only if they secured a solid replacement on the left.

Having done so, it's now a waiting game to see whether the rumour mill has churned truth with regards to a potential cut-price deal for Barcola. The Frenchman has been a priority target for Liverpool for the majority of the summer, as Andoni Iraola looks for further firepower up the top end of the pitch to challenge in 2026/27.

Arsenal, meanwhile, may have to fork out at least £60m if they hope to sign Galatasaray's Victor Osimhen before next month's transfer deadline, according to sources speaking with Football Insider.

The Gunners are also looking for attacking threat this summer, having missed out on Real Madrid's Vinicius Junior following a long and drawn out transfer saga. They could now turn their attention to 27-year-old Osimhen, who has been linked with a move to the Premier League for the past couple of years, only for a deal to fail to come to fruition.

On the other side of North London, Tottenham Hotspur are eyeing moves for Liverpool's Cody Gakpo and Manchester City's Savinho, as a summer of massive spending continues. Reports from the Netherlands suggest that Gakpo has reached an agreement in principle with regards to personal terms, with a £70m price tag being touted for his transfer.

Savinho, meanwhile, has reportedly shared an interest in working under Roberto De Zerbi this season, with Spurs looking to wrap up an £85m move for the Brazilian.

At the Etihad Stadium, the Cityzens are on the brink of securing Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille in an £85m swoop of their own, as Rodri closes in on a move to Barcelona. Having already welcomed Elliot Anderson in a £116m transfer from Nottingham Forest, City have now turned their attention to finding a suitable playing partner for the 23-year-old.

Bouaddi, 18, could be just that, following a formidable World Cup campaign with Morocco.

Stay tuned for all of the latest news and updates in our transfer blog below...

Sports.title: Manager clashes with own fans over Championship star as they refuse to accept new signing
Sports.content:
Manager clashes with own fans over Championship star as they refuse to accept new signing

Norwich City winger Matej Jurasek joined Sparta Prague on a season-long loan earlier this week, but endured a hostile reception from his new club's fans

View 2 Images Sparta Prague's players and supporters clashed over the signing of Matej Jurasek on Saturday night

Sparta Prague coach Brian Priske was forced to step in after Matej Jurasek endured a hostile reception from fans of his new club. Jurasek joined Sparta on a season-long loan from Norwich City earlier this week and made his debut against FK Teplice off the bench on Saturday.

‌



But supporters of Sparta have clearly not forgotten Jurasek’s past with rivals Slavia Prague. Their anger reportedly stems in part from footage from the winger’s time at Slavia in which he appeared in a balaclava while joining anti-Sparta chants.

‌



Even though he was only on the pitch for the final 15 minutes, his every touch was booed, and he was the subject of chants that said 'we don't want you here'. His side’s post-match lap of appreciation was cut short amid the abuse directed towards the winger.

‌



Jurasek did engage in conversation with that section of supporters, telling them: "I'm a young player and I came here to win. I apologise for the statements I made against your club."

Then, after the game, Sparta coach Priske, along with a number of his players, approached his side’s supporters to defend Jurasek. Speaking to Oneplay Sport afterwards, Priske said: "It is clear that the arrival of Matej has caused a lot of reactions in the Czech Republic.

“We all expected it and knew that there would be different opinions around him. These are of course always welcome, as long as they are expressed in a decent way.

‌



"He knew that coming to Sparta would mean enormous pressure and would provoke strong reactions. Nevertheless, he decided to come with one goal - to help us.

“From the conversations we had together, I know that he is well aware of the whole situation and knows that he is not in a very good position with some of the fans at the moment.

View 2 Images Matej Jurasek in action for Norwich City against Stoke City last season (Image: (David Watts/MI News/NurPhoto via Getty Images))

‌



"It gave Matej a chance to express his feelings and apologise to many Spartans. It was a good moment to let out all the emotions that had built up over the past few days."

Jurasek featured in Norwich's first competitive game of the season, having come off the bench in their Carabao Cup first-round win against League One side MK Dons last week. And Sparta will have the option to make the Czech Republic international's move permanent at the end of the season.

"I think those 15 or 20 minutes today showed why we brought him in. Now it's up to him. He has to prove to the fans that he's one of us," Priske added.

Article continues below

"His job is to do everything he can to make sure that all those amazing Spartan fans are chanting his name next year for a completely different reason and in a positive spirit."

Sports.title: New FREE daily racing pullout launched in the Mirror with more tips, news and insight
Sports.content:
New FREE daily racing pullout launched in the Mirror with more tips, news and insight

For the first time ever, the national newspaper is offering racing readers a daily supplement with more racecards, tips, silks, news, insight and exclusive columns

View 3 Images The Daily Mirror is launching a new racing pullout (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

The Mirror is launching a fantastic and free daily horse racing pullout for its band of loyal readers who love the sport of kings.

‌



It is the first time in its 123-year history that the paper has carried a racing supplement every weekday.

‌



From August 17, the Monday to Friday pullout will complement the Mirror’s award-winning Saturday section.

‌



It means that readers will get more tips, analysis, racecards, insight, exclusive columns and the latest news and gossip six days a week.

Our team is the best in the business – led by David Yates, aka Newsboy, one of the most prominent names in racing journalism, who will aim to help readers take on the bookies.

View 3 Images David Yates, aka Newsboy, the Chief Tipster and Racing Correspondent on the Daily Mirror

‌



David will also pen a weekly column – a mix of forthright opinion, comment, humour and the odd tip.

ITV presenter Oli Bell will write an exclusive column every Tuesday where he will tackle some of the bigger issues getting under the skin of punters and racing fans – there are plenty of those.

And Steve Jones, who writes our hugely popular Value Scope column on Saturdays, will share his expertise in a Value Scope Extra midweek column.

‌



View 3 Images Oli Bell (right) will write a column for the Mirror (Image: Karwai Tang/WireImage)

His first column is on Monday and will then settle into a regular Wednesday slot.

David Yates said: “A daily pullout has been a long time coming for Mirror readers.

‌



“It has been talked about for years and has almost happened a few times before.

“We thought the horse may have bolted [pun intended] but I’m thrilled that we can give our readers more racing pages in the Mirror.”

Newsboy and Bouverie have been the regular tipsters in the Mirror for many years.

Article continues below

The Spotform ratings – much loved by loyal readers – will also continue in our racecards and we hope to publish more Irish cards when space allows.

Sports.title: Harry Maguire backs Marcus Rashford for Man Utd stay - 'He is going to help us'
Sports.content:
Harry Maguire backs Marcus Rashford for Man Utd stay - 'He is going to help us'

Marcus Rashford made his first appearance for Manchester United since December 2024 in their pre-season friendly with AC Milan and Harry Maguire wants the attacker to stick around long-term

View 2 Images Harry Maguire wants Marcus Rashford to stay at Manchester United (Image: Andrzej Iwanczuk/NurPhoto)

Harry Maguire says that the Manchester United dressing room want Marcus Rashford to stay at the club following his return to the first team.

‌



Rashford had not made a competitive appearance for United since the fixture against Viktoria Plzen back in December 2024 prior to this weekend and was expected to join Barcelona permanently this summer after signing for them on loan last year. However, the Spanish giants declined to trigger an option to sign the England star permanently.

‌



With no other agreement in place for a transfer, Rashford has been left in limbo this summer with some suggesting he could now be reintegrated at Old Trafford by Michael Carrick.

‌



The attacker featured for 30 minutes as a substitute in Saturday's pre-season friendly defeat against AC Milan while wearing the No 9 shirt, further fuelling speculation that there could yet be another chapter in his Manchester United story.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

And Maguire made it clear that he and his team-mates hope the United academy graduate will still be a red when the transfer window closes. “He can improve us for sure,” the 33-year-old told The Athletic. “I think you have seen when he came on (against Milan), he threatens the back line really well. He could have even scored for us today.

‌



“He’s a huge threat to have in your team, if he’s going to stay with us. Obviously the transfer window is still open, but we hope as players that he stays and he’s a big asset to have.

“I’ve played with Marcus for numerous years and I know that from playing against him, and playing with him in training, he is going to help us.”

Rashford enjoyed a fine season in Spain, accumulating 14 goals and 14 assists across 49 appearances in all competitions for Barca.

‌



View 2 Images Rashford is back in the picture at Old Trafford but could still move in the transfer window

Carrick knows all about Rashford's quality having worked with the attacker both as a player and a coach during his previous spells at United.

He hinted earlier this week that he was working on the basis Rashford was staying put, saying: “He's our player and he's come back great. He's just like any other player.

Article continues below

“I've known Marcus a long time and he gives us something a little bit different. And he's been in great spirits since he's been back. He's been back two or three days training and it's just pretty normal, to be honest. And we're looking forward to the start of the season.”

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
